F94B1FE0DF47429D9507B8DD480B4718.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares. Describe the shares using the words, halves, fourths, and quarters and phrases half of, fourth of and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing (break apart) into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

BCB06A377C6E48488F2E361A2591A9D7.description: Compose (put together) two-dimensional or three-dimensional shapes to create a larger, composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.

96F96A242C104295AA6167C3FB1587C8.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes. Identify shapes that have non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size). Build and draw shapes given specified attributes.

8EB3CA368E3A4A9AA976A3615C3438ED.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

84EEB708B86245409EBE2D9CFF3A5E2E.description: Organize, represent and interpret data with up to three categories. Ask and answer comparison and quantity questions about the data.

7B334320D75F4315965AD86D292539B6.description: Identify values of coins (e.g., nickel = 5 cents, quarter = 25 cents). Identify equivalent values of coins up to $1 (e.g., 5 pennies = 1 nickel, 5 nickels = 1 quarter).

D4A499EEDD1B432E818BAD6AC3A45371.description: Recognize and read money symbols including $ and ¢.

D05D5B34ED514214BB0487916C141A0B.description: Read a calendar distinguishing yesterday, today and tomorrow. Read and write a date.

96D4FB9BDF404D1DBD95B01A7C74BDC9.description: Tell and write time in half hours using both analog and digital clocks.

4E4F36CFE83441D1832D46C6CF5179E9.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.

A17D40485A344DF98D790A35687B6AB5.description: Measure and compare three objects using standard or non-standard units.

E9F0F7715BE846F5921945FAE28F89ED.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

15C2C7BAD1AD4858B7E44CAD2EFD3F63.description:
Subtract multiples of 10 up to 100. Use:
  • concrete models or drawings
  • strategies based on place value
  • properties of operations
  • and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

6575A43764604ABFB13BFD38C34A6F6D.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

15D839A707414255AB53868E74BEDBF8.description:
Add using numbers up to 100 including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10. Use:
  • concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value
  • properties of operations
  • and/or relationship between addition and subtraction.
Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Demonstrate in adding two-digit numbers, tens and tens are added, ones and ones are added and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten from ten ones.

165847D686DE43AE8E80452F3D284F5F.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

4049684A0756479E9ED71D8160956410.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, <.

BFDA6A22A08B4190B5390E8945C0414A.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight or nine tens (and 0 ones).

E74BB4D2FAB04923A4D69374D2AEEF0D.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight or nine ones.

8AC7D356B1D94224800911F3A24C01F5.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones, called a "ten".

FAD6F82EEBF3479FBB9E8696EB54C639.description: Model and identify place value positions of two digit numbers. Include:

6540A36AADBE424DBE274385D0317C6A.description: Count to 120. In this range, read, write and order numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

564309A62454479AAF6A677153E91F8E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

83C5910AE63A4B77AD69C598CEDA7F3F.description: Identify, continue and label patterns (e.g., aabb, abab). Create patterns using number, shape, size, rhythm or color.

2387BE1822BA4BDF944143CBDA01DB92.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 6 + 6 = ?, 5 = ? - 3.

BA0A5065EE2F412DBE8E07FB86D2919D.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign (e.g., read equal sign as "same as") and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
comments: For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false?6 = 6, 7 = 8 - 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2).

2D8644326AB04C8EB374A31E23279ECB.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

CA078FBCADA8420ABFD96B86F0C264FF.description:
Add and subtract using numbers up to 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction up to 10. Use strategies such as
  • counting on
  • making ten(8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14)
  • decomposing a number leading to a ten (13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9)
  • using the relationship between addition and subtraction, such as fact families, (8 + 4 = 12 and 12 - 8 = 4)
  • creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

02DA50D477014CFDBC62DDFD38610209.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

628A1018956D4BA5B009A70AEFC96973.description: Add and subtract using numbers up to 20.

78376FDC575A41D2A95C437D7211EA09.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
comments: For example, subtract 10 - 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

A13CEBA87C37492593543E9E0B398BDB.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. (Students need not know the name of the property.)
comments: For example: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known (Commutative property of addition). To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12 (Associative property of addition). Demonstrate that when adding zero to any number, the quantity does not change (Identity property of addition).

A3F8104693874C9D8666CD1F3AB9FEF3.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

941E04A52C324281BC3234F740D9FB57.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20 (e.g., by using objects, drawings and equations). Record and explain using equation symbols and a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

812FFC3D404B484EA7B563C52FD3020F.description: Use addition and subtraction strategies to solve word problems (using numbers up to 20), involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, using a number line (e.g., by using objects, drawings and equations). Record and explain using equation symbols and a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

50746C6B2CEA4AA3858E8D88C769AC35.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

4E8F4A0E3977429DA17F5B6A300236E2.description: Estimate how many and how much in a given set to 20 and then verify estimate by counting.

D84DF840797D413D9A3289A7AF323C76.description: Use the symbols for greater than, less than or equal to when comparing two numbers or groups of objects.

83BA46CAC03B4B3C88E21365AFDCFD04.description: Count a large quantity of objects by grouping into 10s and counting by 10s and 1s to find the quantity.

14940A4A1DD44034BE32BD39BBF0EB77.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

6BA7B447097546D3ACBCB29E34105C07.description: Order numbers from 1-100. Demonstrate ability in counting forward and backward.

B4C8108E2EE94B6FA88A00DBE9723987.description: Use ordinal numbers correctly when identifying object position (e.g., first, second, third, etc.).

441D59B1E93C48329B0F714A90761973.description: Know ordinal names and counting flexibility.

2AF7D32865064C459F0F8C4133BAD203.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

0BB095AEA7F34686AB93ED5771594B59.description: Look for and make use of structure.

08FA900EDC1F4FE4B3B8E8A3B75DD630.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

B4758B609F814103A51574719B8F1147.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

B89472B0DFE3013127C268A86D17958E.description: Enjoy working alone or with others in a sport or physical activity to achieve a goal.

B8942BE0DFE3013127C168A86D17958E.description: Reflect on reasons for choosing to participate in selected physical activities (e.g., health, challenge, self-expression, social interaction, personal goal).

B893EF00DFE3013127C068A86D17958E.description: Identify several reasons why participation in physical activities is enjoyable and desirable.

B893B210DFE3013127BF68A86D17958E.description: Value physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and/or social interaction.

B89370B0DFE3013127BE68A86D17958E.description: Accommodate individual differences. (e.g., ability levels, gender, ethnicity, disability among people, and physical activities of a variety of actions, culture, and ethnic origins).

B8932FE0DFE3013127BD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate self-control and sportsmanship/etiquette during games and activities (e.g., accepting controversial decisions).

B892EE80DFE3013127BC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate concern for safety of self and others during games and activities.

B892A9D0DFE3013127BB68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate appropriate behavior in physical activity settings.

B89263C0DFE3013127BA68A86D17958E.description: Exhibit personal and social behavior that respects self and others in physical activity settings.

B8922180DFE3013127B968A86D17958E.description: Formulate meaningful personal fitness SMART goals based on the results of fitness testing.

B891DE30DFE3013127B868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate personal fitness by participating in activities to improve specific fitness components (cardiovascular fitness, muscular strength, muscular endurance, body composition, and flexibility).

B8919A30DFE3013127B768A86D17958E.description: Improve and achieve age appropriate fitness standards defined in a selected program (e.g., Fitnessgram, Brockport, President's Fitness Test).

B89153E0DFE3013127B668A86D17958E.description: Compare the fitness benefits of a variety of activities.

B89102D0DFE3013127B568A86D17958E.description: Monitor heart rate before, during, and after various intensity levels of physical activity.

B890B250DFE3013127B468A86D17958E.description: Apply fitness concepts to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of personal fitness.

B88F2070DFE3013127AF68A86D17958E.description: Maintain an outside-of-class physical activity journal based upon units of study.

B8906220DFE3013127B368A86D17958E.description: Identify local, state, national, and international fitness and recreational organizations (e.g., YMCA, United States Cycling Federation, Special Olympics Alaska, Challenge Alaska, and Alpine Alternatives, CITC, BOYS AND GIRLS CLUBS).

B8901160DFE3013127B268A86D17958E.description: Use current technology (e.g., pedometers, Wii Fitness, Dance-Dance-Revolution) to monitor physical activity to meet personal goals.

B88FC000DFE3013127B168A86D17958E.description: Maintain a physical activity log for a designated period of time (e.g., weight training charts, steps during the day, time engaged in physical activity).

B88F6370DFE3013127B068A86D17958E.description: Set SMART goals, (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, time sensitive) for participation in activities of own choosing.

B88EDFB0DFE3013127AE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and understand the significance of physical activity in the maintenance of a healthy lifestyle.

B88E3C20DFE3013127AC68A86D17958E.description: Identify major muscle groups utilized in a variety of movements.

B88DF9C0DFE3013127AB68A86D17958E.description: Implement strategies and safety procedures for success while participating in physical activity (e.g., use a spotter when lifting weights, shift gears one at a time while climbing a hill on a bicycle).

B88DB370DFE3013127AA68A86D17958E.description: Design a game that incorporates skills and tactics that can be played by all students.

B88D5AC0DFE3013127A968A86D17958E.description: Use offensive and defensive strategies while participating in modified team, individual and dual sports.

B88D1990DFE3013127A868A86D17958E.description: Explain at least two game tactics involved in playing team, dual, and individual activities.

B88CD930DFE3013127A768A86D17958E.description: Detect and correct errors in personal performance in a variety of activities.

B88C9A10DFE3013127A668A86D17958E.description: Identify critical elements of skill for selected movement forms.

B88C5620DFE3013127A568A86D17958E.description: Apply movement concepts to the learning and performance of physical activities.

B88C03C0DFE3013127A468A86D17958E.description: Explore Alaskan cultural physical activities (e.g., Native Youth Olympics games and dances).

B88BC170DFE3013127A368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency for participation in adventure/outdoor activities (e.g., orienteering, snowshoeing, skating).

B88B8240DFE3013127A268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency for participation in rhythmic activities (e.g., social, folk, Native dances).

B88B3900DFE3013127A168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills for participation in non-competitive individual activities (e.g., weight training/resistance training, swimming, exercise).

B88AF6E0DFE3013127A068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills for participation in individual and dual activities (golf, Frisbee, bowling, racquet/paddle sports, Native Youth Olympics games)

B88AADB0DFE30131279F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills for participation in modified team activities (e.g., basketball, volleyball, softball, ultimate Frisbee).

B88A53E0DFE30131279E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency in motor and movement skills needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

B40EC2E0DFE301311F0A68A86D17958E.description: A student should understand and be able to form and use appropriate methods to define and explain mathematical relationships.

B40DFE60DFE301311F0768A86D17958E.description: use common sense to help interpret results;

B40DC1E0DFE301311F0668A86D17958E.description: check the results against mathematical rules;

understand and use numeration, including

B8EDAB00DFE30131285468A86D17958E.description: solve problems both individually and with others; and

B8ECE6C0DFE30131285168A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to use technology to explore ideas, solve problems, and derive meaning.

B8EC6FF0DFE30131284F68A86D17958E.description: choose sources of information from a variety of media; and

B8EC3390DFE30131284E68A86D17958E.description: identify and locate information sources using technology;

B8EBF440DFE30131284D68A86D17958E.description: A student who meets the content standard should:

B8EBACA0DFE30131284C68A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to use technology to locate, select, and manage information.

B8EB5FE0DFE30131284B68A86D17958E.description: diagnose and solve common technology problems.

B8EB1EA0DFE30131284A68A86D17958E.description: manage and maintain technology tools; and

B8EA9EF0DFE30131284868A86D17958E.description: use technological tools for learning, communications, and productivity;

B8EA62A0DFE30131284768A86D17958E.description: use a computer to enter and retrieve information;

C9D4A823A5604D87B67657B92D3F6047.description: giving correct and incorrect examples to explain subsistence as a way of life.

B7B91EC0DFE30131265768A86D17958E.description: solve problems by using history to identify issues and problems, generate potential solutions, assess the merits of options, act, and evaluate the effectiveness of actions;

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

document.title: Alaska Content Standards: Government and Citizenship

B7F7B240DFE3013126E868A86D17958E.description: understand that economic choices influence public and private institutional decisions.

B7EA22A0DFE3013126B968A86D17958E.description: know how power is shared in the United States' constitutional government at the federal, state, and local levels;

B7E9E140DFE3013126B868A86D17958E.description: understand the United States Constitution, including separation of powers, the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of government, majority rule, and minority rights;

B7E99D40DFE3013126B768A86D17958E.description: recognize American heritage and culture, including the republican form of government, capitalism, free enterprise system, patriotism, strong family units, and freedom of religion;

B7E942E0DFE3013126B668A86D17958E.description: understand the ideals of this nation as expressed in the Declaration of Independence, the United States Constitution, and the Bill of Rights;

B7E8E130DFE3013126B568A86D17958E.description: A student should understand the constitutional foundations of the American political system and the democratic ideals of this nation.

B7E89A40DFE3013126B468A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast how different societies have governed themselves over time and in different places.

B7E85420DFE3013126B368A86D17958E.description: understand how nations organize their governments; and

B7E80760DFE3013126B268A86D17958E.description: understand the meaning of fundamental ideas, including equality, authority, power, freedom, justice, privacy, property, responsibility, and sovereignty;

B7E7BAC0DFE3013126B168A86D17958E.description: understand the necessity and purpose of government;

B7E75FC0DFE3013126B068A86D17958E.description: A student should know and understand how societies define authority, rights, and responsibilities through a governmental process.

A78F752DCBC64485BDFFA332423C26BC.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
comments: For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.

A06D60CE02DA40DCBB2CA39D45C53CBD.description: Categorize shapes by different attribute classifications and recognize that shared attributes can define a larger category. Generalize to create examples or non-examples.

187B18168D594C3A8A1AC7F001A5006D.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

48691E9D7A5D4EA1A845B69AA248FD25.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions (e.g., by using a visual fraction model).

80711ED0F0C1458B977AD61C46EE91B8.description: Express and model whole numbers as fractions, and recognize and construct fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: For example: Express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6; locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

066798C12D4A47C580AD1DB5AA6B3091.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions (e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent (e.g., by using a visual fraction model).

B6C398958EB84B1F87CCDF3DF13A0D1C.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are the same size (modeled) or the same point on a number line.

24E77127CA4141A895215FAEB6B90B55.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

C0A9B66FBE15497089941C0605FD3C93.description: Represent a fraction a/b (e.g., 2/8) on a number line diagram or ruler by marking off a lengths 1/b (e.g., 1/8) from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b (e.g., 2/8) and that its endpoint locates the number a/b (e.g., 2/8) on the number line.

21E205E27ABD4679A955D2FED0A89D1A.description: Represent a fraction 1/b (e.g., 1/4) on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b (e.g., 4) equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b (e.g., 1/4) and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b (e.g., 1/4) on the number line.

65D7BF53008C4A65ABB6F6D5C6FC183C.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

FA365B7EA7D14DAAB2D8AC178E05999D.description: Understand a fraction 1/b (e.g., 1/4) as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b (e.g., 4) equal parts; understand a fraction a/b (e.g., 2/4) as the quantity formed by a (e.g., 2) parts of size 1/b. (e.g., 1/4)

235717FB0C0F4F69A292F946295F6DBA.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

F8E635BB8AA84F14A5FB09AF6F3059AE.description:
Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including:
  • finding the perimeter given the side lengths,
  • finding an unknown side length,
  • exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas,
  • exhibiting rectangles with the same area and different perimeters.

7B232563A8264BC0AC27DB754E9064AE.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

83E1343D3C2D464AAD5C989C6CA494D8.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.
comments: For example, the area of a 7 by 8 rectangle can be determined by decomposing it into a 7 by 3 rectangle and a 7 by 5 rectangle.

7AB844C29BE94EF19471A433EC9BA574.description: Use area models (rectangular arrays) to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning. Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c.

963F2BB0226A4FEC8460CDB1D60F910C.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

39C86F324FF84677B8D366191E713AEB.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
comments: For example, after tiling rectangles, develop a rule for finding the area of any rectangle.

978585049F314F96A98EA36B7A36F070.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

48F8185980474001A32A8591C3F27203.description: Measure areas by tiling with unit squares (square centimeters, square meters, square inches, square feet, and improvised units).

03596725044240C4B94A6823C18517E6.description: Demonstrate that a plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n (e.g., 6) unit squares is said to have an area of n (e.g., 6) square units.

220B7A25F7934E74A23FAC3B81BE9A20.description: A square with side length 1 unit is said to have "one square unit" and can be used to measure area.

0D89F4D83FE349BEA5A6FE5927A5028C.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

31E05C69899749958932FC6D9E17ADB0.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

D1426356086443A89DAF994436155695.description: Explain the classification of data from real-world problems shown in graphical representations. Use the terms minimum and maximum. (L)

E0DE8B91ED95405DB027B022A3FB0A2A.description: Measure and record lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Make a line plot with the data, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units—whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

E2A22AFEA9F74B58AFB62919F920D228.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

C5FD4F16FC88446E8AC9ED2D1C3EF3A4.description: Select an appropriate unit of English, metric, or non-standard measurement to estimate the length, time, weight, or temperature (L)

88DCCCAF7BF04AED82F04E6766BC0554.description: Estimate and measure liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). (Excludes compound units such as cm3 and finding the geometric volume of a container.)Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve and create one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units (e.g., by using drawings, such as a beaker with a measurement scale, to represent the problem). (Excludes multiplicative comparison problems [problems involving notions of "times as much."])

E7D4658C42A54849AEC2E4B908B8B564.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes or hours (e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram or clock).

7FDEBEB0492645578DB288AEE36C5BD8.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

1AEC6019F1804AAE81E8659BC634222D.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (e.g., 9 x 80, 10 x 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

75D1D1AA905D4A8BA72CEA76038FFF30.description: Use strategies and/or algorithms to fluently add and subtract with numbers up to 1000, demonstrating understanding of place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

C8315FC7FB7342928E5201623A17F02F.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

62F7D7947EC3467F97A796840D4E1FC4.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

FD168807417E4B8AA036D422BD1BFF50.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

9ACBBF843CE04D45AC6DB0A97A9AEAF7.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table) and explain them using properties of operations.
comments: For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.

5FB5A9197DB749A396C8CB1B213D5A4D.description: Solve and create two-step word problems using any of the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a symbol (box, circle, question mark) standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

AFFC9C62FAD94FC3A137F748231BE040.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

F95052755EAA46E18A6C52F89BF8E3D8.description: Fluently multiply and divide numbers up to 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 ×5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

5D818E798CBB4F15B2531C4BAF5C619D.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

4EA5E24248944BF5952FCCC4D3972E25.description:
Make, test, support, draw conclusions and justify conjectures about properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide. (Students need not use formal terms for these properties.)
  • Commutative property of multiplication: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known.
  • Associative property of multiplication: 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30.
  • Distributive property: Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56.
  • Inverse property (relationship) of multiplication and division.

2F5CD9E726B44A058EF5E0B74440ADAC.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

C5E9C3925FFE4E15AEDFE9AAF8CF75BB.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 x ? = 48, 5 = ? ÷ 3, 6 x 6 = ?

762FCD473B7E405C9290885BC43B9717.description: Use multiplication and division numbers up to 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities (e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

E44D58A52EE34E0B8D2F14A5A898FF65.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers (e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each).
comments: For example, deconstruct rectangular arrays or describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷ 8.

CF255D4844C94076BCCBCB312F09B1BB.description: Interpret products of whole numbers (e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each).
comments: For example, show objects in rectangular arrays or describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 × 7.

F76981AAB0534D7EA361443FC8F0A095.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

28D332F4E364470FAD22A6D527FCCC55.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

1E6DB2286D204ECEA2C59DAB82CBC8BB.description: Look for and make use of structure.

5506D0A999CB410AA50646C607F5C589.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

7E67BDEB5A934F3C88C46F5C459A3274.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

B86F8660DFE30131277768A86D17958E.description: Participate with others in a variety of competitive and non-competitive physical activities.

B86F2E10DFE30131277668A86D17958E.description: Participate in physical activities which will allow students to set and achieve individual and team goals.

B86ECFB0DFE30131277568A86D17958E.description: Choose motivators (e.g., music, friends) that will enhance fun and enjoyment in a physical activity setting.

B86E8E80DFE30131277468A86D17958E.description: Develop self-confidence and a positive self-image in physical activity settings.

B86E4BF0DFE30131277368A86D17958E.description: Value physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and/or social interaction.

B86BA7B0DFE30131276A68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge one's opponent or partner before, during, and after a physical activity or game and give positive feedback on the opponent's or partner's performance.

B86E0850DFE30131277268A86D17958E.description: Analyze possible solutions to a movement problem in a cooperative physical activity and come to a consensus on the best solution.

B86DC6D0DFE30131277168A86D17958E.description: Act in a safe and healthy manner when confronted with conflict during physical activity.

B86D8110DFE30131277068A86D17958E.description: Contribute ideas and listen to the ideas of others in cooperative problem-solving physical activities.

B86D3600DFE30131276F68A86D17958E.description: Work productively with assigned or random groups without adult intervention.

B86CF680DFE30131276E68A86D17958E.description: Accommodate individual differences. (e.g. ability levels, gender, ethnicity, disability among people, and physical activities of a variety of actions, culture, and ethnic origins).

B86CB570DFE30131276D68A86D17958E.description: Encourage others by using verbal and nonverbal communication.

B86C6BF0DFE30131276C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize importance of individual responsibility in a group effort.

B86B5CA0DFE30131276968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate awareness and participate safely when involved in activity.

B86B1B90DFE30131276868A86D17958E.description: Exhibit personal and social behavior that respects self and others in physical activity settings.

B86AD320DFE30131276768A86D17958E.description: Experience the protocols and mechanics of a nationally recognized fitness assessment tool (e.g. Fitnessgram or Brockport).

B86A9530DFE30131276668A86D17958E.description: Maintain heart rate within the target heart rate zone for a specified length of time during an aerobic activity.

B86A56E0DFE30131276568A86D17958E.description: Explain how improved flexibility increases the ability to perform skills.

B86A15F0DFE30131276468A86D17958E.description: Choose to participate in activities to increase muscular strength and endurance.

B869D170DFE30131276368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that physiological responses to exercise are associated with their own levels of fitness.

B86983B0DFE30131276268A86D17958E.description: Engage in appropriate physical activity that results in the development of cardiovascular endurance.

B8694590DFE30131276168A86D17958E.description: Measure, record, and compare the heart rate before, during, and after participation in physical activity of various levels of intensity.

B8690740DFE30131276068A86D17958E.description: Compare target heart rate and perceived exertion during physical activity.

B868C720DFE30131275F68A86D17958E.description: Participate in selected activities that develop and maintain the health-related components of fitness: muscular strength, mouscular endurance, flexibility, body composition and cardiovascular endurance.

B8688800DFE30131275E68A86D17958E.description: Apply fitness concepts to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of personal fitness.

B8684500DFE30131275D68A86D17958E.description: Monitor his or her physical activity using a variety of tracking tools (e.g. fitness logs, pedometers).

B867F0B0DFE30131275C68A86D17958E.description: Choose to participate in structured and purposeful activity.

B8679BD0DFE30131275B68A86D17958E.description: Participate in local physical activity opportunities.

B8673430DFE30131275A68A86D17958E.description: Consciously choose to participate in moderate to vigorous physical activity outside of physical education class on a regular basis.

B866A960DFE30131275868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic competence in game strategies and concepts.

B8664150DFE30131275768A86D17958E.description: Use specific feedback to improve performance.

B865F6B0DFE30131275668A86D17958E.description: Devise cooperative strategies to keep opponents from reaching a specified area, person or object.

B865B8B0DFE30131275568A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of spatial relationships with others in order to play or design a small-group game.

B8657A60DFE30131275468A86D17958E.description: Use offensive and defensive skills to obtain and maintain possession of an object.

B8653940DFE30131275368A86D17958E.description: Select and practice a skill in which improvement is needed.

B864F460DFE30131275268A86D17958E.description: Apply movement concepts to the learning and performance of physical activities.

B8624940DFE30131274968A86D17958E.description: Volley a lightweight object repeatedly with a partner.

B861FDF0DFE30131274868A86D17958E.description: Throw and catch an object with a partner while both partners are moving.

B861B2D0DFE30131274768A86D17958E.description: Throw overhand a ball to a target with force and accuracy.

B864ADB0DFE30131275168A86D17958E.description: Strike an object with an underhand and a side orientation.

B8646250DFE30131275068A86D17958E.description: Strike an object with varying force, short and long distance, using forehand, and introducing backhand strokes.

B8641FA0DFE30131274F68A86D17958E.description: Design and perform smooth, flowing sequences of stunts, tumbling, and rhythmic patterns that combine traveling, rolling, balancing, and transferring weight.

B863DB40DFE30131274E68A86D17958E.description: Design and perform a creative dance.

B8639960DFE30131274D68A86D17958E.description: Kick and punt a ball at targets from varying distances.

B8635620DFE30131274C68A86D17958E.description: Perform simple, small-group balance stunts by distributing weight and base of support.

B862FBD0DFE30131274B68A86D17958E.description: Dribble an object with a hand, foot, and long-handled implement in personal and shared space.

B8629260DFE30131274A68A86D17958E.description: Jump repeatedly a self-turned rope while performing different jumping skills.

B8616560DFE30131274668A86D17958E.description: Enter, jump, and exit a long (double) rope turned by others.

B86112C0DFE30131274568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency in motor and movement skills needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

B4012DD0DFE301311EF868A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that advancements in science depend on curiosity, creativity, imagination, and a broad knowledge base.

B400EDA0DFE301311EF768A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that scientific knowledge is ongoing and subject to change as new evidence becomes available through experimental and/or observational confirmation(s); and

B400A980DFE301311EF668A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that the advancement of scientific knowledge embraces innovation and requires empirical evidence, repeatable investigations, logical arguments, and critical review in striving for the best possible explanations of the natural world;

B4005FE0DFE301311EF568A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that historical perspectives of scientific explanations demonstrate that scientific knowledge changes over time, building on prior knowledge;

B40011F0DFE301311EF468A86D17958E.description: A student should understand the history and nature of science.

B3FF6C60DFE301311EF268A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the importance of recording and validating cultural knowledge.

B3FF2840DFE301311EF168A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that some individuals, cultures, and societies use other beliefs and methods in addition to scientific methods to describe and understand the world; and

B3FEE140DFE301311EF068A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the interrelationships among individuals, cultures, societies, science, and technology;

B3FE9650DFE301311EEF68A86D17958E.description: A student should understand the dynamic relationships among scientific, cultural, social, and personal perspectives.

B3FE3240DFE301311EEE68A86D17958E.description: Cultural, Social, Personal Perspectives and Science

B3FDE160DFE301311EED68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of how scientific discoveries and technological innovations affect and are affected by our lives and cultures

B3FD9350DFE301311EEC68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that solving problems involves different ways of thinking, perspectives, and curiosity that lead to the exploration of multiple paths that are analyzed using scientific, technological, and social merits; and

B3FD47E0DFE301311EEB68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of how scientific knowledge and technology are used in making decisions about issues, innovations, and responses to problems and everyday events;

B3FCF2D0DFE301311EEA68A86D17958E.description: A student should understand the relationships among science, technology, and society.

B3FC56C0DFE301311EE868A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the theories regarding the origin and evolution of the universe.

B3FC1440DFE301311EE768A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the cyclical changes controlled by energy from the sun and by Earth's position and motion in our solar system; and

B3FBD180DFE301311EE668A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the origins, ongoing processes, and forces that shape the structure, composition, and physical history of the Earth;

B3FB8A70DFE301311EE568A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of Earth's geochemical cycles;

B3FB41D0DFE301311EE468A86D17958E.description: A student should understand and be able to apply the concepts, processes, theories, models, evidence, and systems of earth and space sciences.

B3FAA070DFE301311EE268A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that all organisms are linked to each other and their physical environments through the transfer and transformation of matter and energy.

B3FA39F0DFE301311EE168A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the structure, function, behavior, development, life cycles, and diversity of living organisms; and

B3F9E8B0DFE301311EE068A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of how science explains changes in life forms over time, including genetics, heredity, the process of natural selection, and biological evolution;

B3F99570DFE301311EDF68A86D17958E.description: A student should understand and be able to apply the concepts, models, theories, facts, evidence, systems, and processes of life science.

B3F8F950DFE301311EDD68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of motions, forces, their characteristics and relationships, and natural forces and their effects.

B3F8B5B0DFE301311EDC68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the interactions between matter and energy, including physical, chemical, and nuclear changes, and the effects of these interactions on physical systems; and

B3F86F00DFE301311EDB68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that energy appears in different forms, can be transformed from one form to another, can be transferred or moved from one place or system to another, may be unavailable for use, and is ultimately conserved;

B3F82A10DFE301311EDA68A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the characteristic properties of matter and the relationship of these properties to their structure and behavior;

B3F7DFD0DFE301311ED968A86D17958E.description: A student should understand and be able to apply the concepts, models, theories, universal principles, and facts that explain the physical world.

B3F74870DFE301311ED768A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that culture, local knowledge, history, and interaction with the environment contribute to the development of scientific knowledge, and local applications provide opportunity for understanding scientific concepts and global issues.

B3F6F790DFE301311ED668A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding that the processes of science require integrity, logical reasoning, skepticism, openness, communication, and peer review; and

B3F68800DFE301311ED568A86D17958E.description: develop an understanding of the processes of science used to investigate problems, design and conduct repeatable scientific investigations, and defend scientific arguments;

B3F63E10DFE301311ED468A86D17958E.description: A student should understand and be able to apply the processes and applications of scientific inquiry.

B8E011C0DFE30131284368A86D17958E.description: investigate careers related to the search for beauty and meaning, which is aesthetics.

B8DFC8A0DFE30131284268A86D17958E.description: make artistic choices in everyday living; and

B8DF8B80DFE30131284168A86D17958E.description: recognize that people connect many aspects of life through the arts;

B8DF4BA0DFE30131284068A86D17958E.description: consider other cultures' beliefs about works of art;

B8DF0C40DFE30131283F68A86D17958E.description: listen to another individual's beliefs about a work of art and consider the individual's reason for holding those beliefs;

B8DECDE0DFE30131283E68A86D17958E.description: recognize that people tend to devalue what they do not understand;

B8DE8630DFE30131283D68A86D17958E.description: discuss what makes an object or performance a work of art;

B8DE4100DFE30131283C68A86D17958E.description: make statements about the significance of the arts and beauty in the student's life;

B8DDF840DFE30131283B68A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to recognize beauty and meaning through the arts in the student's life.

B8DDB4B0DFE30131283A68A86D17958E.description: investigate careers relating to arts criticism.

B8DD23D0DFE30131283868A86D17958E.description: recognize and consider an individual's artistic expression;

B8DC8D60DFE30131283668A86D17958E.description:
examine historical and contemporary works of art, the works of peers, and the student's own works as follows:
  1. identify the piece;
  2. describe the use of basic elements;
  3. analyze the use of basic principles;
  4. interpret meaning and artist's intent; and
  5. express and defend an informed opinion;

B8DC3E90DFE30131283568A86D17958E.description: know the criteria used to evaluate the arts; these may include craftsmanship, function, organization, originality, technique, and theme;

B8DBF9C0DFE30131283468A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to critique the student's art and the art of others.

B8DBB370DFE30131283368A86D17958E.description: investigate careers relating to arts history and culture.

B8DB7260DFE30131283268A86D17958E.description: respect differences in personal and cultural perspectives; and

B8DB35E0DFE30131283168A86D17958E.description: explore similarities and differences in the arts of world cultures;

B8DAF7B0DFE30131283068A86D17958E.description: recognize specific works of art created by artists from diverse backgrounds;

B8DAB3F0DFE30131282F68A86D17958E.description: recognize universal themes in the arts such as love, war, childhood, and community;

B8DA5FE0DFE30131282E68A86D17958E.description: investigate the relationships among the arts and the individual, the society, and the environment;

B8DA1D90DFE30131282D68A86D17958E.description: recognize the role of tradition and ritual in the arts;

B8D9DE40DFE30131282C68A86D17958E.description: recognize United States and world cultures and their arts;

B8D99C40DFE30131282B68A86D17958E.description: recognize Alaska Native cultures and their arts;

B8D95A60DFE30131282A68A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to understand the historical and contemporary role of the arts in Alaska, the nation, and the world.

B8D8CF30DFE30131282868A86D17958E.description: integrate two or more art forms to create a work of art; and

B8D87990DFE30131282768A86D17958E.description: collaborate with others to create and perform works of art;

B8D830A0DFE30131282668A86D17958E.description: demonstrate the creativity and imagination necessary for innovative thinking and problem solving;

B8D7E6F0DFE30131282568A86D17958E.description: appropriately use new and traditional materials, tools, techniques, and processes in the arts;

B8D79EC0DFE30131282468A86D17958E.description: refine artistic skills and develop self-discipline through rehearsal, practice, and revision;

B8D75AF0DFE30131282368A86D17958E.description: participate in dance, drama, music, visual arts, and creative writing;

B8D70D80DFE30131282268A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to create and perform in the arts.

D10157160CE445E9BA977166EB9DF377.description: Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects and use relative frequencies to describe possible association between the two variables.
comments: For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

1BC8B3637EC24D888E4D91784673FA43.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and y-intercept.
comments: For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

571BFE6CE33F4A7BABED91A750F9A4C5.description: Explain why straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

6425FF72398D460D88E3AD84C5DC2E2F.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

115D975D6DC44583859F98CE777675C0.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

6C74BE200AE84BD2B636B365BBAD196F.description: Given a verbal description between two quantities, sketch a graph. Conversely, given a graph, describe a possible real-world example.
comments: For example, graph the position of an accelerating car or tossing a ball in the air.

5AB328EBC5C04BE89A50DDDCA967EA9A.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

365C5ADD7C3445918C4447771B54A446.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

945B1CCC5BD541FCBF62D74D2A9B67DE.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.
comments: For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.

74FF9B4E7E2C4F368EA08F8BC7DA3FC2.description: Compare properties of two functions, each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

88E54B654939445EB1C274B529A6A6AA.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input (the domain) exactly one output (the range). The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
comments: For example, use the vertical line test to determine functions and non-functions.

75FF2B09E84740B7B50933F2AFB6A8CA.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
comments: For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

54893E68C9834B73B0EB96F437E2B21E.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Simple cases may be done by inspection.
comments: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

61BFD198B9AA4C12A572B88D058BF76F.description: Show that the solution to a system of two linear equations in two variables is the intersection of the graphs of those equations because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

DE826D77C7044A0297E1C8838E5A1A2B.description: Analyze and solve systems of linear equations.

26CF0D3C2D7040D8800DB24594239C9E.description: Solve linear equations with rational coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and combining like terms.

F3592E1277864B34B40B0D575777008E.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

A871024BE3F34736AE4553851BFA58E8.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

E9A91FEE65834234988A2A8CAC6DE96B.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

F7FF225A4B2C4A10BBC8744DD20FAAD3.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

EA3B52377E4849BA8AEB7B7FC2C9481F.description: Graph linear equations such as y = mx + b, interpreting m as the slope or rate of change of the graph and b as the y-intercept or starting value. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
comments: For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.

B30DC604A00C432FB6BCE1F94548DB22.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

AE4D5BD27F3F4D2697B88CDC946D8999.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both standard notation and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities. Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

401695679E744C808B9EF204D4B84AF3.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
comments: For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

42CB3A8FD5D247BD98DF18530EE27438.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

04138ED199CA451D9D59BD5B9C273789.description: Apply the properties (product, quotient, power, zero, negative exponents, and rational exponents) of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
comments: For example, 3² × 3<sup>–5</sup> = 3-³ = 1/3³ = 1/27.

2B76C63E82E044B3A86957EDC87C7B5C.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

CFDF7807E6794B6EA8263C94C15D98AF.description: Identify or write the prime factorization of a number using exponents. (L)

888806EA77884F1085ACD9C6875DE02A.description: Order real numbers, using approximations of irrational numbers, locating them on a number line.
comments: For example, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

F6648FBAE3C44C938FA9874622366A49.description: Classify real numbers as either rational (the ratio of two integers, a terminating decimal number, or a repeating decimal number) or irrational.

4851323E197B4EB5B4B1A849D58B075F.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

9B1E26B481CE42648BD0FA696BF3C515.description: Identify and apply the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

C1720D580CDE45E89856ADC4701D6530.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

7E9034522085489687465A1EA58419E8.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

69646A5DB3CD4F889964F139EC6DD78A.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

20BC6E2E0B95446F87DC547FFBDD9B6C.description: Explain the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

23B66DEAFA234E69B55348FBE8CA2E6B.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

A0B4E81A0FDF4F58859BAAD469FFD6AE.description:
Justify using informal arguments to establish facts about
  • the angle sum of triangles (sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180º),
  • measures of exterior angles of triangles,
  • angles created when parallel lines are cut be a transversal (e.g., alternate interior angles), and
  • angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.

52BD4787A96D4582B263F661AA0B552E.description: Demonstrate understanding of similarity, by applying a sequence of translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations on two-dimensional figures. Describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

5BB1730BEE4745F8A8816641B9943D7E.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

5B39DD58662B44B299AA3674E03EA298.description: Demonstrate understanding of congruence by applying a sequence of translations, reflections, and rotations on two-dimensional figures. Given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

770811A076414806B8E4239A08D0A276.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

7396984E454F44498A5784DE2FDAA653.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

064136A4A883460C82C2A5DE1A52BC40.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

03DCD7B8B55B4E34BA7B940F265A8E77.description: Through experimentation, verify the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations (transformations) to figures on a coordinate plane).

0D50455FD9D3491FA0CBC760D339CCC3.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

4D47DBCBB5E841D0991992609819588C.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

5D8A7A3E3DBC4F1AA1830403ACAEDCAA.description: Look for and make use of structure.

3B506E038B84446AB4FAA5825D52C549.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

9CD2517A713B4A37844E10D9E18EAFB1.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

C84DFDFFFCCC49F9893CA1F2BC3CA944.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes me happy).

588671293D6144AABD6E362389BA97A6.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

9704274ECA5543588500C3F03345F1CF.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).

BC12CD08D2BB404FA3DCAB63518A8CF6.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

87279B0B931B411CA5362E1F356CEDCD.description: Use glossaries and beginning picture dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.

E2C5BB910F2B467099DCF779B438C1A1.description: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

5601FC1F04804BC98D400740699C00D9.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition, additional).

F24A1217C04048CD8B4CE86DC1CBDEE5.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).

6F141840416247F5B8CEFDCAAE029689.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

0437777293214E71A942A27D3FA3FDB3.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

88CEF70273A044D0A79913761144880A.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

E5F6D2926C31448780A26838BF49B268.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

DBFE33C96F6E421F9F71DD90813F53FF.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

14E2F80FFEBB434580BB7F6AB72D0221.description: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).

4417D6F5C930415D9517F236D1647AB4.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

F69A5670BB254F85B8EF76E5641F5998.description: Use commas in greetings and closing of letters.

F8BF794918F248AAA4100D5555BB44D1.description: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.

D0E9EBA5B9ED4B14A749B46E2A716FDC.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1CE427AA2A8A45AEB0AB38A1B4D2871A.description: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little boy).

9AE8DBB289664D7B94A1C44025DA693A.description: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

7C4A1A1B401841B3B4B3A973EB8F85F5.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).

DE23E628EB8D4D6FA5CE057F90315EE7.description: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).

8C1543427F424870B893AB367BD3D288.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1C632BC763A348B98AA0E1ECC7CFD7E1.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification. (See grade 2 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations.)

2F698EA4CAD54E35BADAADFF6CAC3612.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

0AC92104F8104A178B212B438010C8CD.description: Tell a story or retell an experience with relevant facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.

B680557F7A184FA4867855DC39D11163.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

EA76F28A0D7D48C5A7039C0357D0DD89.description: Retell or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

4BD7EA8F929F475383B6134CD320B3D4.description: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussions.

E5AA267F2F404DB89C2DE2D253935070.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.

ACAE25F68D024FE28E69729A98517A79.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

507E0CFAD8604F7CBE4345D9D403A6F9.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

24953B3623C7459A9A64F23A92131446.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

3B5C0C55B94744AFB575C9D2EBFF6A8F.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report or visual or oral presentation; record data from science observations).

E56BBD41692B476291721C0D77D2ECFE.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

14A237C1612B418B90C798A46819FE63.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

EE35CBC345244480AE504E14AE016D88.description: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed (e.g., adding concrete and sensory details; elaborating on how the details chosen support the focus) by revising and editing.

8ED74023919340AEA2089190D68BDD47.description: Use narrative writing to retell a well-elaborated event or short sequence of real or imagined events, include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use linking words to signal event order, and provide one or more concluding sentences that restate or emphasize a feeling or lesson learned.

71843F65A3284D15924FB09743F38598.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or one or more concluding sentences that emphasize their most important point or focus.

48D3E893FCA24A048FB96730CAB42393.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion and reasons, and provide one or more concluding sentences that restate or paraphrase their opinion.

9CF3E34B4F4B4F5491C6351A1F2110E9.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

121ED18B9659427A9101D71B4C794BD8.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

A7E2ABB702CC47B3B1DD3DA41497B96B.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

7F846AC9B15D40CBB741BF157BB93D53.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

E384CD42B5964054B97498FE3D52C382.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

84E45A8D830146C78BAE3DB7167B27AD.description: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

AF6D304773E347BBBB8EBC46C7D9A863.description: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

23B7AB881C7C4FEFB9B34966C653A232.description: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.

2A35D124982F41B18F78BE588C8E723A.description: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.

599161D80A6E4F54AD214E15ACF1DF04.description: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.

495CDE3D200F4F199B6DB9EACA4A8520.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

FD5EF9374FCD419697473454EAB3E851.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend a range of informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts within a complexity band appropriate to grade 2 (from upper grade 1 to grade 3), with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

BED83480B97043F3AA04CBFE61581292.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

3E74859E5778498A8B68AC2752D05C7B.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts or related topics (e.g., a book about polar bears and a book about black bears).

3F6AD7D365874DA4ADD1E1B501A4AE6C.description: Describe how reasons given support specific opinions the author states in a text.

6B5D2E19C5BB4AF3B7FB113E0073EEF7.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

E996DB5942684A5C866B4A11A2546DF8.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

BB729A2B714B48DBBA8E7069AFA3FE50.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, headings, charts, bulleted or numbered lists, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

6581DD2AFD7144FCA0BCD7EDA563E32F.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

4C686BA03B8F4CCA9124A4B8332649DA.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

71430B905FF94E5A845A333E88E672D0.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

9BC195962863481096A59E28A0E14C26.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of informational texts using key details from the text.

F48E587DA168463F9611BD8AFBA9A507.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend a range of literature from a variety of cultures, within a complexity band appropriate to grade 2 (from upper grade 1 to grade 3), with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

C4A9797EC83F44D9B1E4D9AACF2667F3.description: Range of Reading and Level of Complexity

8DBC8CB37A464E49B0CE832796E6F8B1.description: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story/text (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.

14B31115A680485C96633E0307060ACE.description: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot (e.g., problem-solution; chronology).

B5A1F57D5AF94720874A0FC6D4F72C47.description: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

FA58AD46876A4687A388771453645813.description: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story (who, what, why, where), the middle describes the problem (how characters react or feel and what they do), and the ending concludes the action or tells how the problem was solved.

6E96DFD0C1EC4B2283B6D747CA3D3313.description: Identify words and phrases that supply rhythm or sensory images and meaning in a story, poem, or song (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) and describe how they make a reader feel or what a reader might see in his or her mind.

B0ADACF541F0497D9276856E1E81955B.description: Describe how characters in a story, play or poem respond to major events, problems, and challenges.

C17958E1A60A4CBD81654953023B664B.description: Retell stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine the author's purpose (e.g., teach a lesson, make you laugh, tell a scary story, describe an imaginary place), lesson or moral.

1EBB0F960CB84581979A493D3EBF8726.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of a literary text using key details from the text.

24624EDBDC2C40348A0EA721C249ABF1.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

43A800694B4242B99CFB8A322618A809.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4CF2021198244CC89CDBC1D0FF813FF3.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

C213DC5014174E8C8E78FAC968D72618.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

20245783D4754C44BA06485E12E5CE83.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

85B6D0E6EF744263BE8B13227064A4AB.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

comments: The K-12 grade-specific standards on the following pages define what students should understand and be able to do by the end of each grade. They correspond to the anchor standards below by number. The grade-specific standards are necessary complements—the former providing broad standards, the latter providing additional specificity—that together define the skills and understandings that all students must demonstrate.

C0E7689E621B49D889071BB9DB62EC96.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

B56BC2976C7B4E22A1188C878A6398BC.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

763B911627F44AB79B730EF0E73516E2.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and that the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
