B7842B20DFE30131263668A86D17958E.description: improve the student's understanding of the student's language and culture through experiences with other languages and cultures;

B783EB70DFE30131263568A86D17958E.description: learn about and experience deep characteristics of the culture, including folkways, mores, laws, traditions, customs, and patterns of behavior;

B783A960DFE30131263468A86D17958E.description: learn about and experience surface characteristics of the culture, including art, cuisine, dance, dress, geography, history, music, and literature;

B7836890DFE30131263368A86D17958E.description: understand the relationship between language and culture;

B7832680DFE30131263268A86D17958E.description: A student who meets the content standard should:

B782DD70DFE30131263168A86D17958E.description: A student should expand the student's knowledge of peoples and cultures through language study.

B7828A30DFE30131263068A86D17958E.description: use two or more languages to learn new information in academic subjects.

B7824990DFE30131262F68A86D17958E.description: use two or more languages effectively in real life situations; and

B7820A10DFE30131262E68A86D17958E.description: write and speak understandably in two or more languages;

B781CD90DFE30131262D68A86D17958E.description: understand written and oral communication in two or more languages;

B7818E40DFE30131262C68A86D17958E.description: A student who meets the content standard should:

B7814650DFE30131262B68A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to communicate in two or more languages, one of which is English.

34E3D1C942434CD4A815F91EE8A9F8B5.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

809E88D6A19D46AB8B80CD8A10757E11.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.

019FE93CA51F4C62800103DCB8F3E153.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).

AE1615D0A11E436F8B61BD2BF4E0DEC3.description: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).

577BEA725B3B471C955AF4C4043037FB.description: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

8A92C5613AAE491BB58B507E25D9114A.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

D7AF0475D69C4DE3993F71132509A3DC.description: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

BC57B5BB742548268C57F579197081D4.description: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).

60A6E1790A9C494B98F237E827A078B7.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.

F9751B91244D415BB4631509EF67C136.description: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.

A10091DB4934442092DB38C3E06969C0.description: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).

172354CB6E5E4DA3A37CF36498B2C5F4.description: Capitalize the first word in a sentence, the first letter of the student's name, and the pronoun I.

8479CF7CEFDA4771A9BD51CDB81AD964.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

1BDA3E31D28A4BFB9C4F41D5B4F95FC2.description: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.

56611AB37C6A4F4993E59CCF65DCD118.description: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).

7A037D29B33D450DA32383CF8481CC88.description: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

346235BC91A54F61866A87A1DFA2EE3C.description: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes).

FF392AA1529C4880B9612DBBF3FB3EAF.description: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.

C45E0E4013F548AEBFA2E4629D3DB515.description: Print many upper- and lowercase letters.

8FDF4EADD7D2415F93E7B05A92D01846.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7765D25C1CD344C9BDD0D132F57C7B9F.description: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

1F2685C2354F4AE3A732A2F86BC5498B.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional details.

8B913C61EB904B3589B21B5922E607C1.description: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events, and with prompting and support, provide additional related details.

37591612BD084949A2DF0F69D27C5101.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

F8D97AD588AF4631B5935ED81AFE7926.description: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.

7BCE90F2A57D4C3582D9B7AB0D6E29EA.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

7BD03FE76E7F42FB834437CF00154433.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

6824AB199777474691BD306F17D7C808.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

9F72B7EFF51D4F24A243FC8A4A7A4422.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

A2C4A81402A14C4F93802B38B989BC26.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and combine or summarize information/facts learned or express opinions about them).

8BBC03C86B324564907406230BA93142.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

8ACC204315374AD5B3D3E48D8FAD9CF3.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

293A65346F26459983CAF5AAA8A40AD3.description: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

6243092E38DC4193AE4B38699EF0254A.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a real or imagined event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide an ending (how the problem was solved) or a reaction (e.g., a feeling) to what happened.

9D478CE23C0246808BC3D62FDFBA9E16.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

EE4B193DFD7741D9B4FDD79E01767527.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to state an opinion or a preference about a topic or part of a book (e.g., I like dogs better than cats because…; My favorite part of the story is when…; I think it was funny when…).

86C0013614A347C696DE60ABD148AC94.description: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

C218116441584766ABD401A15FF52B08.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

06D66F0CC20B465EA332B2886E57A9C2.description: Read common high-frequency words by sight. (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).

562085A403294774964D5F61486D8D46.description: Associate the long and short sounds with the common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

F7A6F05AD6384D34B0333806414F54BA.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary sound or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.

24E8310072124F5B92DEAB82208AA62D.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

127D8649C380497E9C0999198E6163AC.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

1025FA2E0CCF4ADAB9574F6248C8AE2A.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonant-vowel-consonant, or CVC) words. (This does not include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.)
comments: Words, syllables, or phonemes written in /slashes/refer to their pronunciation or phonology. Thus, /CVC/ is a word with three phonemes regardless of the number of letters in the spelling of the word.

FD864208849248FEA3C901646372903B.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

1E6D72B1B3F640FD96C63E0159873962.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

FA65942942574BBCA1C19D255EDE8A65.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

118B038C7E3B4A3FB15FB400E18C34AC.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

61762C75A9C4432094D38D943112D89D.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

6051D23ABB8D488FB8CA538A610C9BF1.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

9598DF93C252403AAF6F975676CECC26.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page-by-page.

E5D1CF5A5B9F4C9881E08C9F25633940.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

40874A3F10CE403A8593A5A46681C6A0.description: Actively engage in shared reading activities using a range of topics and texts with purpose and understanding, with scaffolding as needed.

1304ED5C1F2F4FD59D76A5BBA13C2B71.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BC8E61E016574769AF239626F37FB26D.description: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between information presented in two texts on the same topic (e.g., compare two photos or diagrams, compare two animal babies).

A94AF85E95594495B6E56D7BD0F92DD2.description: With prompting and support, identify the opinions an author states in a text.

273E214E10DF450C87E415FFA56EA05D.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).

8B0359EF59DE45A09184BB3F5188A0E7.description: Name the author and illustrator of a text and describe the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.

944B8EAD94CF4A458DD48D41B0BDE217.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

92B33EDE338F4149AB9F9F361CAEA960.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

38DA3AE835E74B2AA1461B4D090FF485.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

3F9953AC25734FED8CC68A04AB34B5B7.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

EB57DA9A626344DE8E9BB63871C2ABED.description: With prompting and support, elicit background/prior knowledge and experience in order to ask and answer questions about an informational text using key details from the text.

F00DA9BE67C347CDA418F55581BB1DD7.description: Actively engage in shared reading activities using literature from a variety of cultures with purpose and understanding, and scaffolding as needed.

0A7F44892FE443C0A3F89E1B2F0476C3.description: Range of Reading and Level of Complexity

42935FC5CD7A4BAEB9DBEE4BAA27FEE5.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

904FA644266146F5B6F6B192ED88C007.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts) or use illustrations to tell or retell a story.

2D7C0E3D87BA4EEAAF7C27D8BB7AC96A.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and describe the role of each in telling the story.

5F8D83FC053E4045864FE21DD4AB5774.description: Identify common types of texts (e.g., picture books, stories, poems, songs).

7EE3B93251084726899776CA9EF15C5E.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

9306DB8662304D09BD5D3D00CFCF9361.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, major events, and problem-solution in a story, song, or poem.

1FF21DA8CE54483FAD6B0128D00F49BC.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, using key details.

D79AF3138B7C43069A5A0E6D1F01B195.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about a literary text using key details from the text.

76E78E57F54C4AEA9284EDB4EC34D92F.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

8FFC2438210A4BBB80097298604850A2.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

EF651C61209A4CAEB7C4B665663AC7BF.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4C37D926B2584494B886B1620C734FF5.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

A40C54E541D643BA84995DC1E90D5061.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

2DE9A56A70204FE6A41A3A6207C412CB.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

127B4346753043F1A325F04CAFD43540.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

75E479458E8B4128A79926E3434C2955.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

E873DB68117A43CFBBA9A8C94D51B095.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and that the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

47A3F5CE560145EEBE13C6996E065251.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

693EBC6A65704E4BBDFD978D52DB8C65.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

4240CF39B43342F6A39ECD488C1E21A0.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

0080C1BCA6154FAD882A62D6F3CB2A90.description: Alaska Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening
comments: The K-12 grade-specific standards on the following pages define what students should understand and be able to do by the end of each grade. They correspond to the anchor standards below by number. The grade-specific standards are necessary complements—the former providing broad standards, the latter providing additional specificity—that together define the skills and understandings that all students must demonstrate.

2C97023279B849F58775C87645614445.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

74153893B7CB44079863E8760AF957BF.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

3A2CF911805B402B91DC337AEA7A6245.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

6F1A3C32285845AEB414C722D8C8C4CA.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

6B10B998AAAF486B922302B5C0E5BB54.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D76E9367528A463D91CF92710FDA0A96.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

B50BDB1E4311407BBC79C60E633D82E1.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

8E771D1B6FE54AE1B5A5A898C70E5B39.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A206253ECAD24417BA1156EFAFAFCAB3.description: Use narrative writing to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

B5FA3CEEA65641E59A21075B95C70DE1.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

E9D969A43E63471599B453558D9D5AC3.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

comments: The K-12 grade-specific standards on the following pages define what students should understand and be able to do by the end of each grade. They correspond to the anchor standards below by number. The grade-specific standards are necessary complements—the former providing broad standards, the latter providing additional specificity—that together define the skills and understandings that all students must demonstrate.

ACCD1E234F614D95A788D9A9562A8E18.description: Read and comprehend a range of complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

4E616F26E13342CBA982BDAC6900E76B.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

5043CD93087B4D358444C09BE502B5C8.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

05045B3306654AACBFC1B49298171FEA.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

3BE9699094B74F6D98F27C4FE20B4DAB.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

66DFCE247D90413F81CAC78486EF70A9.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

EE1F013983F347569018F85B1EDC30F0.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

F1A32F57CCA446D5BEB8E76541A1E984.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

7FAB2F53B363471C9022B71D453169CC.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

E5AB2881C82D4EFFA46573BDEFEE5392.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

F2361795B9E5494CA8890AAFD209549E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

comments: The K-12 grade-specific standards on the following pages define what students should understand and be able to do by the end of each grade. They correspond to the anchor standards below by number. The grade-specific standards are necessary complements—the former providing broad standards, the latter providing additional specificity—that together define the skills and understandings that all students must demonstrate.

113C2DCC3FCD404792E9CF1D3690B757.description: Classify two-dimensional (plane) figures in a hierarchy based on attributes and properties.

24030220086943289693388D206810A7.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional (plane) figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
comments: For example, all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles.

2552E098BD964548B57979E208D75591.description: Classify two-dimensional (plane) figures into categories based on their properties.

47958AF4730D41109076C458FB9BB2E9.description: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

8BC292549CE742CCAB80616BFE92E95D.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

0D1651546C3A4C9583355AEC56264BE5.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

0AF22ABB9EDF46098ECF4F7A00DAE4CE.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem).
comments: For example, how much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 1/3-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?

536E5338CCF44026B57DF98F05305B03.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5), and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.

5FF2BF4A6ED04C43A7B8855C556B6E2E.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.
comments: For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4, and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.

EE4D26832E364F96A500BC0145AE740A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

556172E9C01D49E8B3DEBA5EC6D8E454.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers (e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem).

07F1E05DDD4B44B9868C691125E65181.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n × a)/(n × b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1. (Division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade.)

745828498C7B460DB8499FCA6C81F5D6.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

E69420D16A2A476AB4165F1F935912D8.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

A20C8100BA494BC1B7BBC6C2C7193CA9.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15. (In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.)

F403A6115FDB4CCE87D10BE9230E67DF.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

83372226FD5C437B88F462F8C2D60CB3.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers (e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem).
comments: For example, interpret 3/4 as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that 3/4 multiplied by 4 equals 3, and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size 3/4. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

5E66F8069CD9472CA3507A9F0A117966.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

3D9B3072A1FF40539B01DD0C3A81FE8B.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators (e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem). Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and check the reasonableness of answers.
comments: For example, recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7, by observing that 3/7 < 1/2.

EF6D1F5BD5664B6EA196ADDF9C43763E.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.
comments: For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12. (In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.)

40E37BA4F41B48B58F48F66CEEA42051.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

ED8D0AAD95134A5C87AE3B0D2374BDC1.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

10DF22189BE544E484532EE22CDACB58.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h andV = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

B3D844B44C5F43AF95D32575D88BEA5C.description: Estimate and find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Demonstrate the associative property of multiplication by using the product of three whole numbers to find volumes (length x width x height).

ADD354CBBD0F4F0ABA56463B761B8CA9.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume.

B9E8E217ACB94E569D689105FDD1DF4F.description: Estimate and measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and non-standard units.

FD5DCAEEF0DA42019425F703851A76EA.description: Estimate and measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and non-standard units.

4E959FD31AF340C5A08868694BF4CD9B.description: A solid figure that can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

2F1EBE2E5C41407ABB5B5893DE89AC98.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

E6C3866290654CB78A09A0A1D20B526E.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

884B4BC7E98F41D6A942F62ED983A9A8.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

3BCA975A771B4297BCE997BEA47D776E.description: Explain the classification of data from real-world problems shown in graphical representations including the use of terms mean and median with a given set of data. (L)

4C7C4B251F7841F58B64F785A862B8D1.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.

0666A46BC56D49F6A4B9BFFE918B88CD.description: Solve real-world problems involving elapsed time between world time zones. (L)

5AB89E87E0434E0B8ED6A771266FC89A.description: Identify, estimate measure, and convert equivalent measures within systems English length (inches, feet, yards, miles) weight (ounces, pounds, tons) volume (fluid ounces, cups, pints, quarts, gallons) temperature (Fahrenheit) Metric length (millimeters, centimeters, meters, kilometers) volume (milliliters, liters), temperature (Celsius), (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real world problems using appropriate tools.

8DB6DFC1B9D2414EAFF4EA10E1D62921.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system and solve problems involving time.

1EA5848C2CD04CFAB6320C57803C9DB0.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between the operations. Relate the strategy to a written method and explain their reasoning in getting their answers.

63B8938130BD4A96B7AD2A67220D6365.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, number lines, real life situations, and/or area models.

4989D35142BD4D16A44BFC1730096DD7.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using a standard algorithm.

0CFA394292D244268737F0E123697BF4.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

36232049CB7B49FE8329844ED7608954.description: Use place values understanding to round decimals to any place.

ACCF0D9292BB49668739E0E475A60139.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths place based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

61254C8EA9FC4F4AA25AF597F2E68412.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form [e.g., 347.392 = 3 x 100 + 4 x 10 + 7 x 1 + 3 (1/10) + 9 (1/100) + 2 (1/1000)].

5B4C50839D174E52962954A3A6AAC184.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

9A35FC38A3D242C4AE59CA1F558A1EDC.description: Explain and extend the patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain and extend the patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

193406EB690D4369A1DD95214279841F.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

9E4F11F4F0554562A5A9F9A85BBB6D27.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

403EFCAA1F904134872D9DF1888D894E.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.

AA66387770694B17B6F77C8173A667AA.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
comments: For example, express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 x (8 + 7). Recognizing that 3 x (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.

1EC9807D50C049D7A2B11C0469B2A9C3.description: Use parentheses to construct numerical expressions, and evaluate numerical expressions with these symbols.

F34BB7F2FD2A4AD8890C5509CFB4740D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

116C7BD8F7654F3F8D570A98392282CF.description: Look for and make use of structure.

8837B2F6FB6643379DD02D56BDD0425C.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

DCD4D03A2CCE4FC0A600680A6424DC1B.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

6A918020D1B944AFAAA9B10A196B8AB0.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.
comments: For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?

1080A0DEA26643229E25489C548531AC.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

40C7838409CA42F4BE1CC65C7918E477.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

315F6E76B9DC478DAB8D82A8AD56E0DC.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

FE1D9148882443F38D562E03828F1027.description: Design a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.
comments: For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

FBDEFFEEAA5A43AC9B652EF254EDCA9F.description: Design a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
comments: For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.

02D1A29047274CAAA8791056FD4DDA35.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

9AA530E588094B539A0785808DD171A4.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
comments: For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

9B396F77D4154FF682B6877D8C7455F3.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

70AA6DD2FA794FC3AF38019946C2A7CB.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

E39CA168268F4D79A4C68BBA906E8B99.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
comments: For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

880DA09EFF5645CBB166A485D2779D1B.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.
comments: For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.

5D12B8F8F65649EDB43BD6712071A13F.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

2FE218D1A523479C88DF676E2CF11492.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
comments: For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

ECB058D56F6749D0B0AEEFBC865D982C.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a reasonably sized sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

D3C95779E0DF457784E471CB1490DA82.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

DF3637E956814B499F13E56823F30569.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
comments: For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

77A0C5D4903442848BABDE9D7A0E75BF.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers.
comments: For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

1AD6C74B55DB4BD1A54EDC203B65E898.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct multi-step equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

4EE105688EE14E05A5FF54D02782286A.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.
comments: For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

058012EE889E439A94230F1F45CE9928.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

3E69F3BD949348FCAF4D62DD758EF905.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.
comments: For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

1FB8B7F3266A44638C156554DA383AA8.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, expand and simplify linear expressions with rational coefficients.

4CEFDC5F51234829867B61E6E67DD761.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

C3FDC64CA72E4A86A803EFD49F63E232.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers. (Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.

1F322C4A8084419C90C08A9743DD9D4E.description: Convert between equivalent fractions, decimals, or percents.

018E2EA3F12449489C0FDEA8852A1C17.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

8BEBBC25DF504203A3540CA12A8B48CF.description: Apply and name properties of operations used as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

14416702926D435C9718BB2ADFDD501C.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

54DB3986DEC64DB784B4135D858C1A21.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

BE45CCF5158145A3B7A1E0B263E54DE8.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers and use equivalent representations.

906A978944514B3EABC0016D79E69706.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

C8F40AE474F54D0394858A9CB7981B4F.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

2E470BDD5F6B45EFACB2D7B698E6CA0F.description: Understand addition of rational numbers (p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

1CC274FE65CA47A5B158ECB77D332AA6.description: Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (additive inverses). Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.
comments: For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.

A6DE498FE7B342989D993C62B6707F63.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

3102ADED108D43A2A6B8D5888C4AEBAB.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

D96EB24814A244CAB6AF6D6943EAE7F3.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.
comments: Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

B649F1F5D1A64CC6B5A0BFB7F5FAD895.description: Understand the concept of unit rate and show it on a coordinate plane. Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

E47C8494B0A349AFBBD48D5F0D89D4D2.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations and multiple representations such as tables, graphs, diagrams, sequences, and contextual situations.
comments: For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

4F3E46706CA64D7DB360EFBF832019DC.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships in real world situations.

2FC81845113245ECA4E1D99A40F2E1AF.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin).

E706252E27934DA4A33D23E6177CDE66.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. Make basic inferences or logical predictions from proportional relationships.

BE2FC0EA370C415092616056C30ABA9B.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.
comments: For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2/1/4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour or apply a given scale factor to find missing dimensions of similar figures.

799E7ACD2F96412C85ECFA992895455F.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

5D1C0C6445AE4C09940A21835FFC2DA8.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

B9024644CBB34CD9803307ACD5FAECF8.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

240BF7AB586F4B76A70A24E0AA2B050F.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

99618B0B8C8048288C6A445FE1E80377.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

1EA3793F245249999EE9FFA1A82F4F27.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures, i.e., cross-section, that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

E0A8C4405E514494B9B42491374F2FA6.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes including polygons and circles with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

9EDB39A465A84FB3B704EE6C8DAF7C21.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

49860C1918D24D0CA6F12725094F9FBC.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

8574B0D8AD1E4576B261434258E7BC8D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A35F1E38C1FA4F7B85B5F2195B04FB76.description: Look for and make use of structure.

48AD762087C84648A6FA3ED70A0C421F.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

7229F35D18B141E9AD6E5373DA793F6F.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

B8A5D270DFE3013127E668A86D17958E.description: Analyze selected physical activity experiences for social, emotional, and health benefits.

B8A55230DFE3013127E468A86D17958E.description: Recognize physical activity as a positive opportunity for social and group interaction.

B8A595B0DFE3013127E568A86D17958E.description: Recognize physical activity as a positive opportunity for social and group interaction.

B8A50550DFE3013127E368A86D17958E.description: Seek personally challenging experiences in physical activity opportunities.

B8A4ADB0DFE3013127E268A86D17958E.description: Enjoy the challenge of working hard and the satisfaction of improving skills.

B8A46370DFE3013127E168A86D17958E.description: Value physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and/or social interaction.

B8A421D0DFE3013127E068A86D17958E.description: Exhibit sportsmanship/etiquette in all physical activity settings.

B8A3E000DFE3013127DF68A86D17958E.description: Accommodate individual differences. (e.g., ability levels, gender, ethnicity, disability among people, and physical activities of a variety of actions, culture, and ethnic origins).

B8A39C80DFE3013127DE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of responsible personal and social behaviors in physical activity settings.

B8A34D20DFE3013127DD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate leadership by holding self and others responsible for following safe practices, rules, procedures, and etiquette in all physical activity settings.

B8A309F0DFE3013127DC68A86D17958E.description: Exhibit personal and social behavior that respects self and others in physical activity settings.

B8A2C7C0DFE3013127DB68A86D17958E.description: Design, implement, monitor, and adjust a personal fitness program to meet personal needs and goals for a lifetime.

B8A28650DFE3013127DA68A86D17958E.description: Compare and identify fitness value of specific movement forms.

B8A24240DFE3013127D968A86D17958E.description: Assess physical fitness status in terms of health-related fitness (cardio-respiratory endurance, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition).

B8A1F190DFE3013127D868A86D17958E.description: Meet the age and gender-specific health-related fitness standards using a nationally recognized assessment tool (e.g., Fitnessgram, President's Challenge, APEAS II – Adaptive Physical Education Assessment).

B8A1AA10DFE3013127D768A86D17958E.description: Apply fitness concepts to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of personal fitness.

B8A15280DFE3013127D668A86D17958E.description: Develop evidence-based personal activity plans that include self-selected physical activities and sports.

B8A11740DFE3013127D568A86D17958E.description: Identify local, state, national, and international fitness and recreational resources(e.g., trails, wilderness areas, rivers, lakes, National Center on Physical Activity and Disability - NCPAD).

B8A0DC50DFE3013127D468A86D17958E.description: Maintain an outside-of-class physical activity journal based upon units of study.

B8A0A0A0DFE3013127D368A86D17958E.description: Use current technology (e.g., heart rate monitors, tri-FIT, Dartfish, Wii Fitness)to monitor physical activity to meet personal goals.

B8A02620DFE3013127D168A86D17958E.description: Explain to others the importance of strategies and safety procedures for success while participating in physical activity (e.g., weightlifting, wearing a helmet while snowboarding).

B89FDEE0DFE3013127D068A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of major muscle groups to improve performance and/or create training plans.

B89FA2E0DFE3013127CF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize various levels of performance (novice, competent and proficient).

B89F66C0DFE3013127CE68A86D17958E.description: Identify basic biomechanical principles as they pertain to movements within a physical activity.

B89F29A0DFE3013127CD68A86D17958E.description: Acquire new skills while continuing to refine existing ones.

B89EEA80DFE3013127CC68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of complex movement patterns, independently and routinely, to improve skills.

B89EA660DFE3013127CB68A86D17958E.description: Utilize basic skills, tactics, and strategies while participating in a variety of lifetime activities; and advanced skills, tactics, strategies while participating in at least two lifetime activities.

B89E57E0DFE3013127CA68A86D17958E.description: Apply movement concepts to the learning and performance of physical activities.

B89E0D50DFE3013127C968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills while participating in adventure/outdoor activities (e.g., Alaskan cultural physical activities, hunting, fishing, skiing, biking, hiking, wilderness survival, camping).

B89DC8D0DFE3013127C868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills while participating in rhythmic activities (e.g., Native, folk, social dances).

B89D8460DFE3013127C768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills while participating in non-competitive individual activities (e.g., walking, yoga, aquatic water safety, Native Youth Olympics games).

B89D3E90DFE3013127C668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills while participating in individual and dual activities (e.g., golf, tennis, bowling).

B89CF4B0DFE3013127C568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competent skills while participating in modified team activities (e.g., soccer, lacrosse, hockey).

B89C9980DFE3013127C468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate competency in motor and movement skills needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

E6F573BEA4CE45B5ABDED8B07855364B.description: develop and use citations and bibliographies.

5D2CABAD207041118869DC0AB15FA1FF.description: understand and respect intellectual property rights and copyright laws; and

8A3DCAC8CF3D4E2EADE6EDECD1EE54C8.description: understand and respect the principles of intellectual freedom;

8C13B06638E54031A15FBC3F6755E24F.description: use library materials and information resources responsibly;

E914A2EEE7344CE6B22E46F1D808011B.description: A student should understand ethical, legal, and social behavior with respect to information resources.

53A21C911DE44BB1814848F059283887.description: assimilate and understand how newly acquired information relates to oneself and others.

B42CF72713B74EC2B0DFCE6833508ADA.description: evaluate information representing diverse views in order to make informed decisions; and

DDE08A966E054ADB9B09462FD7959DA9.description: access information on local, state, national, and world cultures and issues;

6397AFCEEB55479FBFFFEFC3EBA9BF6C.description: recognize the importance of access to information and ideas in a democratic society;

990A60D83CB64514B538BFCE917C2D08.description: know how to access information through local, national, and international sources in printed and electronic formats;

B7E94FED1B044512AF92ECC12B27659B.description: A student should be aware of the freedom to seek information and possess the confidence to pursue information needs beyond immediately available sources.

1141F67A59624E748675605F69FEC3E7.description: recognize and select materials appropriate to personal abilities and interests.

0AC568EC48E546E5A45EBCCA9A594551.description: read, listen, and view a wide variety of literature and other creative expressions; and

0B9BCC230C7C4420813458107710FE08.description: A student should recognize that being an independent reader, listener, and viewer of material in print, non-print, and electronic formats will contribute to personal enjoyment and lifelong learning.

590C42286F2440CD95E74A7950A34DC6.description: evaluate the effectiveness of the product to communicate the intended message.

BA3323D61D934D419228F91221818433.description: organize and use information to create a product; and

94D5A51DD6D643FB9B44FB65F59147F6.description: evaluate the validity, relevancy, currency, and accuracy of information;

A55E106FC5494B14B7CE6F41427DF6CA.description: consider the variety of available resources and determine which are most likely to be useful;

45987BBDE8BE4A6F882A5E23347FA213.description: state a problem, question, or information need;

D00673D0562E43F881837C29609CD489.description: A student should understand and use research processes necessary to locate, evaluate, and communicate information and ideas.

DD1087662A31422983914C3616402169.description: identify and use search strategies and terms that will produce successful results.

03795F0E3DCA482193F7829ED4732603.description: search for information and resources by author, title, subject, or keyword, as appropriate; and

6365E2413C56427382A0F0C7AED25DB2.description: understand how information in print, non-print, and electronic formats is organized and accessed;

BC0A832B344949D991DF81D243C0458F.description: understand how library classification and subject heading systems work;

24AA42F8815642A6895D72F2E579E724.description: recognize that libraries use classification systems to organize, store, and provide access to information and resources;

32BE2C88C914465D99F410794013B6C5.description: A student should understand how information and resources are organized.

869057352F064EB398E3FFDC0AF2464E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional (plane) figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

4662C742B4DA4FC5B1B10F5C336BEBFC.description: Classify two-dimensional (plane) figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

4E5B863B6C5C46DE9A847AC84AA368E6.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular, parallel, and intersecting line segments. Identify these in two-dimensional (plane) figures.

1A47C26C23B34C589E18B2B4992E0C4E.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

EE7E982E0CDB4C22B47CE7706A5B75E9.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions (e.g., by using a visual model).

4F3320971C154EBB902F1CE32AFA2F8D.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

7A8595C73BB448579C9DF735D0FFEEF8.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
comments: For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

0B3F339650DD404F8EEF921FD13D545E.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

C4F9E0C8B2AC41BE8F58BE183C138B17.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem). Check for the reasonableness of the answer.
comments: For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

F07114B18CB040E98F03D37B333B762E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

E59780E158764DA0A10DE3E5D870529C.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

B05141395CA249698A2355544A8762B4.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

6DD63FA1FFCF48F3AF7E131917C7D9D1.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem).

B9952151B8944560A5AEE2F5B6D7F03E.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators (e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction).

298BF7BE95BB41938E4655AACA669053.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions (e.g., by using a visual fraction model).

DA0AF61E280A4547A3170E5AC3684336.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

5560B996CF8B4CCD8EBF8CB8CCC31250.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

CEFDB41B303B4F739640FB3A7FB5809F.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

3672EA12C3354182AD21AC07E76CF8E1.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators (e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2). Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions (e.g., by using a visual fraction model).

076EC8728EAE4C6BB7367953131D35E8.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

D9E40BEE0E844F7595A226A6D83DD070.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

223D9528D73748C9BEF7DC64699726F3.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is divided into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems (e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure).

3C5E9FFA4F754E8CB46831A54DB042B2.description: Measure and draw angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Estimate and sketch angles of specified measure.

996EFA4CC14645D7AEDF2E0F1EF6DF93.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

AF82BE3F094E44FBBB6EEF1BA91A302E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

902A94B66DF14CF4B4B80055710537C0.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand the following concepts of angle measurement:

6FFEF630841F48C092CE9D0FA1DC1120.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

2072A133FC884D4DBCB98964CC6F4276.description: Explain the classification of data from real-world problems shown in graphical representations including the use of terms range and mode with a given set of data. (L)

938D587826E2498BA8D9D8AC85D6ADEF.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

57E11CAE0764427AB6563712CF0FB0B1.description: Solve real-world problems involving elapsed time between U.S. time zones (including Alaska Standard time). (L)

8C2B37E3BA16438F8E128F5DB668136D.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

E8C34A59816C40E9B89FC4CDE4C94ADF.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

F15F0D97453E420684FAFFB70FF4E920.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4-ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36).

0FC54287DBF14C8F8BE6AD9FF16CCF7A.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit, and involving time.

74DE52550F864A4FB3FB5E6815202D86.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D860151869EB48AD838DCE2795D9E302.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

B415622CD8414C86A8C28C3D653CD405.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using any algorithm. Verify the reasonableness of the results.

C2EEE8470A1342EE9726CB578E36FF38.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

D9D342C19F8243E1ADCADD6EF8C044AE.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place using a variety of estimation methods; be able to describe, compare, and contrast solutions.

D5A4A5DBE71A49028DB2FE8178F0A966.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on the value of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

6DF588C6199F404E9A791DE581AE79BA.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

7E39326E85D34C7FAD2AE06174C9A7DC.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

D8F9045D939B475BB2B4D360D6269AA8.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

58C94CB5DD12487DB620BC27E8F05142.description: Extend patterns that use addition, subtraction, multiplication, division or symbols, up to 10 terms, represented by models (function machines), tables, sequences, or in problem situations. (L)

9E9FE111C3384B9D9B955821792DBDB1.description: Generate a number, shape pattern, table, t-chart, or input/output function that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. Be able to express the pattern in algebraic terms.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

27029E1D53A24CBE86E296685DF50957.description:
• Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100.
  • Explain the correlation/differences between multiples and factors.
  • Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number.
  • Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

22AB1F0E5EDF4EA7B20F798CBCA81409.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

A0DDBAB6736E4E88B664DBC8ECB2D8B7.description: Solve multi-step word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

10F7F12D49344A0F8FFBA94565AE984A.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison (e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem or missing numbers in an array). Distinguish multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

9F4AC716959840CB9B0916609F05FD0A.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 groups of 7 and 7 groups of 5 (Commutative property). Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

8B043FB9FC9849E7B98CDD3282C23F0D.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

139F37BB12B04DF692B6B631463E223A.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

EC4DC1FF84874BF29354FEED10CBAD66.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BB48EB0D9D9A48399F47C8A55EAA00D0.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

1BAFA7931B9D4DEDADBCC17A632C6569.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

05A5C14811014C3ABD45DA57A3863F64.description: Solve or identify solutions to problems involving possible combinations (e.g., if ice cream sundaes come in 3 flavors with 2 possible toppings, how many different sundaes can be made using only one flavor of ice cream with one topping?) (L)

E9C8B710CC1F404C82071A6B5877369D.description: Analyze whether a game is mathematically fair or unfair by explaining the probability of all possible outcomes. (L)

79FD936EFEA24AD0B59B38EC68331413.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

A93077A7C897442CB1B2746A65DAF823.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range), as well as describing any overall pattern and any outliers with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

8716ED5A23C54908B093158D4E564CE0.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

22FEE9F75354405E8B5495385E03AE88.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

8D9CB8F1DF674330B97A5823FAFB04AE.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot or line plots, histograms and box (box and whisker) plots.

95995284E7C8492ABFA1308A989BE8FC.description: Recognize that a measure of center (mean, median, or mode) for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation (range) describes how its values vary with a single number.

B6DCB389F1284FF894297D56838972A8.description: Understand that a set of data has a distribution that can be described by its center (mean, median, or mode), spread (range), and overall shape and can be used to answer a statistical question.

50D2598FB51E4CE29C2DFD6937D0F130.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.
comments: For example, "How old am I?" is not a statistical question, but "How old are the students in my school?" is a statistical question because one anticipates variability in students' ages.

1A11A7A08D654743851E3B2A3E2BC4BF.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.
comments: For example, in a problem involving motion at constant speed, list and graph ordered pairs of distances and times, and write the equation d = 65t to represent the relationship between distance and time.

0CC9B94E95D24656A4846067C892134B.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

8B3A9129446F40939726988BDB6E91CA.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

82156CA1DE684271822FE8762AE9722F.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

BB902D12758C4946A8991EADF07DB6CB.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

C91B4C7CE1354A5B8D36D8AB914279D6.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.
comments: For example: does 5 make 3x > 7 true?

4BB4A625E8744D8CB739834C6688853F.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

834AC1222E66485FB77A819682A1C872.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).
comments: For example, the expressions y + y + y and 3y are equivalent because they name the same number regardless of which number y stands for.

1A2C2858993745F7AEA00747D41F9D3B.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions. Model (e.g., manipulatives, graph paper) and apply the distributive, commutative, identity, and inverse properties with integers and variables by writing equivalent expressions.
comments: For example, apply the distributive property to the expression 3 (2 + x) to produce the equivalent expression 6 + 3x.

B1D14068CB5846CC8FF8CC984EAA0BD2.description: Evaluate expressions and formulas. Include formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole number exponents, in the conventional order with or without parentheses. (Order of Operations)

037C5E0C72DA42C0868D81BB068FAB57.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.
comments: For example, describe the expression 2 (8 + 7) as a product of two factors; view (8 + 7) as both a single entity and a sum of two terms.

731C5E4730F045729B9ABE9FC0BF2755.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
