comments: For example, express the calculation "Subtract y from 5" as 5 – y.

4C831ACE272D4B35AB033587A639A163.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

90D9A66AF2AC4FAAABC06A434A9E80B2.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
comments: For example, multiply by powers of 10 and products of numbers using exponents. (7³ = 7•7•7)

F4A940889DC64EBA9570232DD73FEEC8.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

D9C9BE21393E46F9B496B702F65A23F5.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

6C68088EBF4047218289B23220409204.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.
comments: For example, recognize that an account balance less than -30 dollars represents a debt greater than 30 dollars.

23AE09F1646A44A7A75FC9EC4762B708.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.
comments: For example, for an account balance of –30 dollars, write |–30| = 30 to describe the size of the debt in dollars.

AADD1F09320B451D939620F68F1DB2FD.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.
comments: For example, write –3 oC > –7 oC to express the fact that –3 oC is warmer than –7 oC.

5C0011846C6347A5916C3B5842197386.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.
comments: For example, interpret –3 > –7 as a statement that –3 is located to the right of –7 on a number line oriented from left to right.

AA2CE89C5BB34A228820370354CA30E3.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

17495A875AA0490E8F5D713534D3E665.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

D9B93BA0019148B28496E7E4755A63C5.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

087F1C5383034154B558480627B1F5FF.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; Recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself [e.g., –(–3) = 3] and that 0 is its own opposite.

508750AA4C8C46919ED121297FF2D202.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

4B3BBD45C347444E882F9721DC1F3B48.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explain the meaning of 0 in each situation.

FB8A1D6FCADE43A09F01DB1F6249B159.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

C534A8A7AB774902804348089E54C9C8.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.
comments: For example, express 36 + 8 as 4 (9 + 2).

059150FA6CB04684A1E455D9B8D5D9A5.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation. Express the remainder as a terminating decimal, or a repeating decimal, or rounded to a designated place value.

1C182FAAD89A40B5BA4CADCC4C61685A.description: Fluently multiply and divide multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm. Express the remainder as a whole number, decimal, or simplified fraction; explain or justify your choice based on the context of the problem.

6814AA37BA424A8290F107D65413BAF1.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

BB24B91769C2417C855E65B0115AC2B8.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions (e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem).
comments: For example, create a story context for (2/3) ÷ (3/4) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient; use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (2/3) ÷ (3/4) = 8/9 because 3/4 of 8/9 is 2/3. (In general (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = ad/bc.) How much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 3/4-cup servings are in 2/3 of a cup of yogurt? How wide is a rectangular strip of land with length 3/4 mi and area 1/2 square mi?

FFFD38DE8E8B47918F2F6BB14E25CCD1.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

D89240A528424643A52995AE645B9C41.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units between given measurement systems (e.g., convert kilometers to miles); manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

58DB760570E641E8B54BC85E7C73B244.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

FA62AB40A8ED42BDBDBB6475B5342827.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.
comments: For example, if it took 7 hours to mow 4 lawns, then at that rate how many lawns could be mowed in 35 hours? At what rate were lawns being mowed?

9BD1DC437B2641C38A6D07FFD7403F5C.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios, and understand equivalencies.

784C3FC531344786A888C9BE1136EC25.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems (e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations).

A8A741F0AE194FF4A637193FA4CF4E2E.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate (a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship) and apply it to solve real world problems (e.g., unit pricing, constant speed).
comments: For example, "This recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of sugar, so there is 3/4 cup of flour for each cup of sugar." "We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers, which is a rate of $5 per hamburger."

2DC2A8962CBC430989672660936ABF61.description: Write and describe the relationship in real life context between two quantities using ratio language.
comments: For example, "The ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the zoo was 2:1, because for every 2 wings there was 1 beak." "For every vote candidate A received, candidate C received nearly three votes."

A5695EAB2F6246BE9E143877807D2991.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

EF4224E052F44E97A9ADA87BC00F7B6D.description: Identify, compare or describe attributes and properties of circles (radius, and diameter). (L)

8DD230CF820746F38A9E6C988B8E12B0.description: Represent three-dimensional figures (e.g., prisms) using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

278FA417B005427F8C48587D3ED4DBDD.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; determine the length of a side joining the coordinates of vertices with the same first or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

F894BF2935944BAA86A23DD88B360C71.description: Apply the standard formulas to find volumes of prisms. Use the attributes and properties (including shapes of bases) of prisms to identify, compare or describe three-dimensional figures including prisms and cylinders.

B49C3401C93D412E8221E4917D3CDD2A.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing or decomposing into other polygons (e.g., rectangles and triangles). Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

658C73A8B2284050B1F2045289C30E92.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

DC8D28BEE86847BCA0AFA86F8DC74AD9.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

2FE9586EB4B24E52989993AE2A71A221.description: Look for and make use of structure.

C7D86007A95542C197A1BCFB6F098C24.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

1552062D11BE497991C02BF9BF427166.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

B8CC7EE0DFE30131282068A86D17958E.description: identify resources available to support education and training related to career possibilities.

B8CC3C70DFE30131281F68A86D17958E.description: identify education and/or training needed for career options and advancement, and develop a career plan; and

B8CBF540DFE30131281E68A86D17958E.description: use labor market information to identify occupational and economic trends and opportunities, and evaluate possible career options;

B8CBB7C0DFE30131281D68A86D17958E.description: identify possible career options, considering both employment and self employment, and understand how changes in the workplace affect career choice;

B8CB79B0DFE30131281C68A86D17958E.description: identify and appreciate personal interests, aptitudes, abilities, and priorities;

B8CB3AC0DFE30131281B68A86D17958E.description: A student who meets the content standard should:

B8CAFB60DFE30131281A68A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to identify career interests and plan for career options.

B8CABAF0DFE30131281968A86D17958E.description: understand employer and employee rights and responsibilities.

B8CA6B40DFE30131281868A86D17958E.description: understand the need for safe practices in workplaces; and

B8CA2300DFE30131281768A86D17958E.description: understand how an individual job fits into the overall organization and how the organization fits into the overall economy;

B8C9E930DFE30131281668A86D17958E.description: understand the process for developing self-employment opportunities including marketing studies, business plan development, and managing business finances;

B8C9AE30DFE30131281568A86D17958E.description: understand the process for seeking employment including résumé development, application completion, interview skills, and appropriate dress for work settings;

B8C97300DFE30131281468A86D17958E.description: understand how to apply skills and academic knowledge in a variety of work settings;

B8C93610DFE30131281368A86D17958E.description: develop and maintain a work ethic necessary for success in the workplace that includes honesty, integrity, dependability, punctuality, self-discipline, initiative, reliability, accuracy, productivity, respect, and perseverance;

B8C8F610DFE30131281268A86D17958E.description: A student who meets the content standard should:

B8C8ABC0DFE30131281168A86D17958E.description: A student should be able to develop and be able to use employability skills in order to effectively make the transition from school to work and lifelong learning.

E05FD188A2C24C0D9ADC7F50BF80DF3D.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

7932CB6896704148A05DCE36AA090394.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

0919F42EAE754B4384D2F663849EAE64.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.
comments: For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.

FDA4CC19A14249B28E02A333EA14588E.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.
comments: For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast-food restaurant.

6DFE1EBC4EE2446DB804506A8C4B2F49.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

4FB9D5E8E1BD416280B8A95CD2DF8914.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

4BD5BC2CDE3A48E6B5C9F780AB3369B3.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.
comments: For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?

93D0FD115FD74B369AD60840785DBBDB.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.
comments: For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

90F7136BCD4E4CF285E4E3378415C093.description: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

4B2006270DD04EEBAE207003182762DD.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

1DAFCE2D53DB411AAFDADE536AE9A6A9.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

210DF9841D5F4C4894217D5B7B4C4CFA.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

5F5599E7F6D941D3AE0518138BC0629A.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

B379822D037A48FCAE014B6069F442EE.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

5679466B567248BBB9C4164291A5F6DA.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

899C3DDE04174668908A87CD643C4F50.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

E96138A5B6354A4F9B121176078C336A.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
comments: For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

47F6CD1D646041D3802BFE22B2702351.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.
comments: For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in 10th grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.

7688509DAA8D44B1910A1720CD9E1053.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

C236A5B7D71C4264A5746DC861A81E51.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

A91EFDB5DEC3426EB537A05A8FC3F2C6.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

454F68D0E01B4F6691A0322AB4BFDC62.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

CC84C7C04E434B4687B1C0130495D154.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

D6D1F426E0154AACB83F51EE748AEE81.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

133F396B4CBB43C1A3FE58CC1351887D.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

BBEF87106E7549808D7684C3FC483217.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

FBD64F713F5340BB9E16C55F480A0071.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

1B3F19B1F3ED4B39BE8969327FC7AAB7.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.
comments: For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

A97CE476EEF84D528683447D5EFED4C6.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

FA37F6C216F34506AB2F70533DE270AC.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

F0B9B4841E004C71B26CCC8ADAA300A2.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

AE5951A882E34082B8C54C5305CB193C.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

12C44075EF4B460F8B821DB9CF4B87B9.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

F5CF3F4B3C894C3DB19D5050043E2727.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.
comments: For example: Describe solutions to problems that require interpolation and extrapolation.

6BE64BF2DA2C484081D81008285C9D02.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

78A906F47D544E1AAABB33AAB83384D4.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

B7ED8524ABEF42D3B3B435D99304CFDC.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

EB89131D19ED49B28EDA8921A00BEC6C.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

792E595F1387472C870EB8CBBB0CC8D3.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

D46879600D1A4CD489B7DE5BA17BA86F.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).
comments: For example: Justify why median price of homes or income is used instead of the mean.

568CB973173A45B6A7B32B36487315ED.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

672386AC36B64611B5D88AA96A3AD506.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

788A2F29D68B419CA6169A3CCCCD2EB7.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

36D2AE1E4D70476585FD44468D043BF2.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

124FF7D278084035815D2B3AC0802749.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

5CC9CEC04EB04DD5BE7F3FBCBDEAFFD2.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

1EAB4C426A4E46729AD72D01448AAF25.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

6EA1805C31ED423BA20391D337EC9686.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

9C4A26019DA14054B0FB2B1468F2252F.description: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects.

C671CE48ACCD4F8A99CF396E45FDC9CD.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.
comments: For example: Solve problems requiring determination of a dimension not given.*

3F0028ABE55541C2B33F1D134E85484C.description: (+) Give an informal argument using Cavalieri's principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

C97B83C4480B47D6B14E4F7C77FF8E4F.description: Explain how to find the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

8728804C3D05426CB0C4EEBE7EC6C697.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

899C8337A9964A8EB5A4F03E61A82445.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

6761DDF5624B4083B0DFB9B119C44330.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

9498436BF6B04746B05E6979520E0632.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

comments: For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

B533DF6DE5394F189DBB23294F202EC0.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

2B16B6A9380C4A13A8A0642E1FE74F93.description: (+) Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given foci and directrices.

819B3D9FFBF44F9B9EAAE5CAB04A465B.description: Determine or derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

710D113276B74402ACD5F697994355A2.description: Determine or derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

D0B79FEAC1D84AE79B4B90A9A4FF3700.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

1F9B9BFB6D0643EFAF9389A8A10B5EB9.description: Use and apply the concepts of arc length and areas of sectors of circles. Determine or derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

183D0AAC754F49BB9819F5F3A8481F55.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

C56C33386FAD42DA84D397BDB3675949.description: (+) Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

4F28D10D78DB476E8316E38EA726BCFE.description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

8431EFA8625D486280AB95C0D2828015.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

2031A983B1A847D3B13978B7B4446FC8.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

C196552A93E84045A3B210CB9C0B0758.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

55D7A0D7D0C24D598F82CCF14ED452FE.description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

59721F61AE154F80BBA8F078397E2407.description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

C580D092C40342429F0AD41471CF93B6.description: (+) Derive the formula A = 1/2 ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

33E8158DD1B945D2AA8816D274EF9974.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

4109DFC609BD4B539FF671586E9AB3E4.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

704F8466F9234D9FBC488F8CFA9084D9.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

FD5119D6B9D94B42B5FBBBF9189855AD.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

1AD334CEA6074863A4D401E95450EFD8.description: Apply congruence and similarity properties and prove relationships involving triangles and other geometric figures.

2052AE2BDEE3467DA1157A5C0BF01D49.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely.

7D06656A93F447408CF579E4FE7A9A4C.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

DEB31EDFD315450885D88DEA8A080370.description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of transformations to explain whether or not they are similar.

BCCA004068BB43ED93F721A6C48226D3.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

A19CA3F13E464D4D9C9A462C68A807D8.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

3322BEDD9BB04212920DDA2C120E625C.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor:

BFE7A44A522E493AAB1EEA9F50B6E33A.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

105004F3E9B3439484F2A6A0E013D6F4.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

A312CA1666944AF3A45C86477808710B.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

21E9500D2C2D4FCE8D9867CBBE82A852.description: Using methods of proof including direct, indirect, and counter examples to prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

E6F5CB1FD4214841A784FEF19354B66E.description: Using methods of proof including direct, indirect, and counter examples to prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

BE6DD6BBC4FD4E04A7E5535B2C139FE0.description: Using methods of proof including direct, indirect, and counter examples to prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

645DA139468149F591CA1F8A81BB668A.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, SSS, AAS, and HL) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

83A568919A814E4183C690CB8B02CE3C.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

4A1CCCF3C8104EFEBB318AB82749F0F7.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

FFA7F1B5EC804A3CAE7FA56FB2B9E02A.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

D4C3A162FCB44876B861393A8EC8ED86.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

86DE39F72AF24797A608B01A2C4525CC.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

2D4BBE06062C4B32837B9D5C886B723E.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

9FA832CE262242B18596584C7E0CDCF7.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

380C3549BB3D43DCA8AD0CD0ECA56084.description: Demonstrates understanding of key geometrical definitions, including angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, line segment, and transformations in Euclidian geometry. Understand undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

D947EC3887684F48B3D8ED45831D819B.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but rather in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by an asterisk (*).

8EDF3AB53D624208B6C76485B2A18B04.description: (+) Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.

8DA9E231EC554AB79DCC81CD33488E84.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to calculate trigonometric ratios.

0F474BB4D25E4EE6AB00B92118FEF0DF.description: (+) Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

5A5D5A7E7CF346C99FDF32A295CD31FA.description: (+) Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

0CD6A4118D644ED4A0B8251C2300A3C7.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

E9F90C0D64B24B04A84E57182FD129BF.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

941FD86D722848A399CD1A3E28BAD8E0.description: (+) Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

E7496944259743168865EDB89F369527.description: (+) Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4 and π/6, and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosines, and tangent for π-x, π +x, and 2π –x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

0A94A22C5E0747B298251C615CE4D64C.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

2771FA821C8341CDB5FDCE2CF1F82BBE.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

B5166FDBBF8043B2B4BFA158B8847007.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

738236BB01D5460B86E71E4FD780EFAB.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

872142D5BF604B7CAE0588DE3D9D1F2A.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

D89B5F1D73EB44649226A64C6F7A9329.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab<sup>ct</sup> = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

6DE28483A1654494B6C8EE8979FA49F0.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

DCD61E97240146DB9ADE9883C279D1E0.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or input-output table of values.

1360FCEFABEF4C40BD8B50CD30151E24.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

5418D2F1BBAB4B8A8AB23B16236E3219.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

572815306FBE474EADCB2CBBA4163E31.description: Show that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

9D32D4BE2C354EB984F18AD4B8BDA7F0.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

0621DC3C119C496E9D42FA91D3CDA140.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

177A8981E6D64B00B81FB0EF76C5DCE9.description: (+) Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

A9DF89496A11418B9065FF7859B2C5AF.description: (+) Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

C0931514E2424B078B2E3FFD21BCC58A.description: (+) Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the function has an inverse.

610E8DA9302C494380C1C7A145E681D1.description: (+) Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

943DD01D76594F52A000126DE78DECFA.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse.
comments: For example, f(x) = 2x³ for x > 0 or f(x) = (x + 1)/(x – 1) for x ≠ 1.

E6F106CA6EEF47EEB30074FE210319C8.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

9138219C30A24FCEA6026078A94A40F8.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

C9EA7949509C4A28B97659489391F667.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

comments: For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

E68966B218274966BCDC3C398DDCB627.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

D3C4ECF2234145F3B8263EE841027F91.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

EBAE8E19D0CA43CBB6771785D5864AD7.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

B9BDB4840A7B4057BC050156D2955F8A.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

3CFF37F60FD74A3798828908C49A1814.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically, in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

3075FDAEF6C94F558A509E5EBD62C91F.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)<sup>t</sup>, y = (0.97)<sup>t</sup>, y = (1.01)<sup>12t</sup>, y = (1.2)<sup>t/10</sup>, and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

5B4EFEB2DE534F4C9395105D5B16179C.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

2D6FFF48B2D14485A8E3CA88CF5C260C.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

068C52E52B8B4FD7A2ED6190C5CAA0C7.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

CECA7DE7159648D69A8E52B565365FB9.description: (+) Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and discontinuities (asymptotes/holes) using technology, and algebraic methods when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

7CFC23C399AB4DBAA1D0CEC113120FC2.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros (using technology) or algebraic methods when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

20C2EF6E2596447AA2DC9E39754F3E3F.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

A4958AB41D5D4A4B86185C4F48B864D4.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

4426D9BF9C4E4D1B819396B473C57195.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

B5D9D990FCC64B61AE21F9E1C6C7BA9B.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

AE355079DC8F4231B5A2D60AE3CB1F2A.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then negative numbers would be an inappropriate domain for the function.*

2DEB4209E60C4FFF883F765029A48EE5.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two quantities,
  • interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and
  • sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.
Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

9035A32A0868469DBB0A6A71EBC73A40.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

FC7348F53C2C4EE99293D58148603010.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.
comments: For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n ≥1.

DEE055F043D448469086BC4AB25B885D.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

D203F64385A849CC8AD8A0DEF97230F4.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

02CC2EFE746A415AABA42F306443BF1F.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

F2E86F0E2B2B4A5F8C5FDCE7423DA11E.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

C3136A2286064DB08959A0BA2AE274B6.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

285A5C6AE59D4CA1B5B62EFCF7634B88.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

5422C0D897924EEEA814FF3ACC2059F1.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

BC7E325229154FF6824FBE754A6CB377.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

BC26B4EE656D4FB6839096E05B24FC85.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

B56A8218375F4FF581EC5BE6679056FE.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

E1EB54DDB54A42039D59F5853C60B7EA.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately, e.g., with graphs or algebraically, focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

F5E0802D135245449904FE11DD1BF258.description: Show that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

9562313A93CB44B493DF3562B0F10F6A.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

ED08A00FD2C54E999C8AECEEA7301732.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

AE6D8B49758648858A8317DFF047ECFD.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

41747C2225D2476580795BCB90D7AD82.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

67F206447C6444469289331AB9F39937.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

3081050662D14AFD943BE190EECB7DFE.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

3CDAFD38AE4E4DDDB4A7D0060DE69EBB.description: Apply properties of mathematics to justify steps in solving equations in one variable.

36AB8D2A7DFD4B889643DB2E4BEDDD7A.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

A957BD8447474B0ABF55696E0BE6CE3D.description: Rearrange formulas (literal equations) to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
comments: For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

6B1C365570C646B6AA1BBDEFD76B1623.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
comments: For example, represent inequalities describing cost constraints in various situations.

2B388E6E5B4F42EC803B199AAD647490.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

11A5D225BB9F4A12B2B8509DB21E1850.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

88548957F2A74A7EAD2FBEDB63EA6236.description: Create equations and inequalities that describe numbers or relationships.

09668D49B9D34A80869FA18F86E8CD29.description: (+) Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions. Understand that rational expressions form a system similar to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression.

D81D3D42104A4320B44F8F15A959F7F2.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

6896A318691F43CCBC0EFFA778DB85C1.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.

62B8198ACCE94A26810FEBAF166AB9B9.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

F9EBEF7CF38B43A88CCB9040D5615AA7.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

9DFBEE6FB6A646C883FD1FB173AC7EF7.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

6F361CD790B041C0A10CDBDA64E049F1.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

043A4D890D234BEFB29827ED58072124.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

4C4693F7913C4D6B9781EAF209A7D4DE.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials. Understand that polynomials form a system similar to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

1CC268116F674029A25B1D6854086183.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

72603580DAA64F0793978B569BF2C3B1.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.
comments: For example, calculate mortgage payments.*

81016B7AD2314508A06191405A23997A.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example the expression 1.15t can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

D1724617B6AD45A1BED684E13C75E222.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.
comments: For example, x² + 4x + 3 = (x + 2)² - 1.

B26960147BCC4B62A4453D7A143BA4AC.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.
comments: For example, x² + 4x +3 = (x +3)(x +1).

D333FEC3C81F4346B9BA80342B57E7EA.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

1D6D7A3B63FE4A5BAB33C080370CFEDF.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

93F5CD075D67420A859A55A1CD230494.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).

73220B03CC9A42E59730CA8660A341A9.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1+r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

B866D675D6B84B009FB72FB6BCEEEF0A.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

1754D98E7A94410CB40BA5FF2E7E0C93.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

1B52CA0163CC4417A640C3B93592EC69.description: (+) Work with 2 × 2 matrices as a transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

53E7792C92F342F4B0FB7D925AACF7FE.description: (+) Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

7ECF632B38A840D4AA57324F2721C635.description: (+) Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

70BE736013DC44D1A03C0B4E26A54B6D.description: (+) Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

C9832E92F7074D4998F740DDA98A9B16.description: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

C46899174CEB459EBD68EB76CDE91883.description: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.

1C5391AD75E440B6B290064847E854A0.description: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

87B4BBDAF8AA42788A175A3660E62669.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

26CD64FF399B4D15AD8CAC8EF44DC633.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

16CC1C08C326460AA5020A55BFC8CF1D.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub>, cv<sub>y</sub>).

85652616E77046C9849B73DC95AD0D8B.description: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.

EDBCC1F6940D4CF58027BAE98F8ED6E4.description: Understand vector subtraction v – w as v + (–w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

97CAF808487C4EB396BB17B656407BBC.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

3C69248C9AE44EA28EC0D3C917C1D01B.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

00AD8F349A9545BEB384CD5AFD8B2BAC.description: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

585119664F9343C0B9953E7D1C350E22.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

F94E3C3CE594403E95655D3E353913EF.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

B9B9EF63E88C45B7BC2ACA277C8A64C7.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

F5A461EB89E246E7BD8FA2B751505F1D.description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

58E8BA3958BF4A979461BB68E0554FAD.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
comments: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).

C32647ECD2344B4480BD0EFD4156E199.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

F8D2CFC7FDA74513A9BF0E055F9AEBB9.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

8378FAA42924441387E67F9958E6337B.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

D2A32C86986848DF83D8008EAFC1B6F1.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.
comments: For example, (1 – √3i)³ = 8 because (1 – √3i) has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

C9A9F418E5BF4990B3FF0A35D24C1A67.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

1422230996CF4B1CA2DFCEF81158F623.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

E94F7F22CFB847F8909269A530095064.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

36FE5B1317244030830EEB7692E0F23E.description: Use the relation i² = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

766EC6E0F0784B4092B7F3E2CCA845EE.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = –1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

989974AD686D45E08321AF1810F4AFE7.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

BF9DCF8CCDF04B2D8EBC40B035F46F3F.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

650E9DD730FE420A9A61D82B9C50F866.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

E2B439F111374680A793C74359ECE001.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

57D26299AFFB4E80A421073EB55C63B1.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

B5D963B0BB0547E799BE193D753503CB.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

7728352EA3A7427380B9CEACA57E6FB1.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

06E0361E01AD4948A2EFCF0C7B47D8FF.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
comments: For example: Write equivalent representations that utilize both positive and negative exponents.

AB64F2EB1B9D4450AD5C36D73DE9EB14.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
comments: For example, we define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.

8AB18179E9B544ED93D3DA2456CEEBEA.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

F3171D6A5F334F678B7A8664971C320F.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3A7CBAB7CAC84BC6A02F7378C887A8F7.description: Look for and make use of structure.

2C90EDAD06A4438BAF84EFD6952DDCB3.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

BB1B8C0989F043B59BEBF5AA9A0BB14C.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

comments: The Standards for Mathematical Practice describe varieties of expertise that mathematics educators at all levels should seek to develop in their students. These practices rest on important "processes and proficiencies" with longstanding importance in mathematics education.

4C1CA509559B4C9BA9684C7DDB2C69EF.description: Acquire and accurately use grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

8EC17C7D13C143339D8A14CDFD387F28.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words (e.g., words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty, such as knew, believed ).

31FEB383CE364014A4FCA1E3A7FF1740.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

43C70C14B9BA4F6385182496AC33C8E5.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

3C7245D6C1824705B2FF68DB21C99BAE.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

201F2C089317493085E6B5C9D98344F1.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

597004A6920245D28E3F05C43A3CF1DE.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

83F65903384A46478E51E5E2491EBA8C.description: Determine the meaning of a new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

4F98B8602F664E2F9D074759DD1653EE.description: Use a sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

AB4190254EF046BE900075E5ED473A78.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

333D731B9E744ABCB8CCC3F04970AB1F.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

91832AF4A85042A2888C9A4092DF08BB.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

2667B2DAC62148159551821FF3297D35.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

5B8E8152FA7A4D18A5F524656BE2D811.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spelling.

0BA38CCD9E79476DA95BC613133D2651.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

623F1DB449CB428998E2B7EDC520F677.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness)

5F28BEDCC9C24EAAA5542890D1DF84B0.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

723C8E699F28467AB92B03E966A50068.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

6B2DAF5471DE4709952535B003ABCEC6.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

F5A5BF84A41F4692BF00A58FEA9582C1.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

FB08394971894030A5519B4CA0070BF6.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

824FEB1CF02F4CE486F6728E04A9EE35.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

C3391C4326DB46DDB436D20AD2835D95.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

A221E3693B0B4043A654109E03629C62.description: Use nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs appropriate to function and purpose in order to apply the conventions of English.

8B7958D60FB6418BA5F900874E844920.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

1C3C7571466842DC890BC0F42BCF8DC3.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification. (See grade 3 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations.)

68901DAD7C314B90B363B84928EAF8AA.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; use techniques that engage the listener (e.g., inflection, different voices); and add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

27C10F5EAD5F4FACAE15515A4A5E9533.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

1CA0D19087994195ADDAD692F7E9690E.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration or explanations and detail.

B8FEFC4B2CC245F0B742E740E1088305.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

B82693274CAE4B1899DEAECC604E29D4.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

3C5873FCCCF24A6D8A8D264D703BA140.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

81DD070C91654273BD30046FEE3A4380.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

F553D70D320648D6AE48B9F7EA71F513.description: After learning a protocol (e.g., Socratic method), come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

D707ECBB0A4F45238E68FB134D4AEE7F.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

9CE98CDD12194D0BBA72323F263C9E64.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

C7AD870E8C214F7CAB6C1BF4F32A3947.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

7368FF9D38E54B65ADF3F0CB2A7FBEA3.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

17BE296E1E0643748AA7941208F2060F.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

9D5D2F1A1456422585D1088F7DE8E223.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others and to locate information about topics.

EBF69DA179C54E309C245D9700F6D14D.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grade 3.)

6B1E3FDA747E45D181AF6455D227FE38.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–3 above.)

0ABD2F23EC7B43AFAD74D42C5D23A8BD.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

472D1E5C7588407EA76C99E03B3FBDF3.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

E244092DF8744FB58D8D5A2C638762BF.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

519661BAB3474CB8B21E8D2075EDDC79.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

4700AF1E5B2D4D64BB9EDDF6690C4AC1.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

79017EBDD05648F98301E43D31F50875.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

11D0B7EB5153462E8642B3C0A47EF216.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

88B0F5F3365649808F78303D6FD76DF5.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

87B590324F174BE7B6AD2FB525BFCBB9.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

9DD1A65329AC49D5952A1D303F7E4787.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

4D160CCE27A94A05BF0AAE9FCF5A7A42.description:

By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11–12 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

5DAA0C226FD54E2CAB39684EF668111B.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful.
